metadata.title: The Harvest
metadata.description: A repair pilot on a routine spacewalk is plucked out of orbit by a living harvester ship. He wakes in a cracked pod among a thousand stolen specimens. Earth is next on the list. Get out, and get home.
metadata.author: ai-generated
metadata.credits: Voices and sound effects by ElevenLabs (elevenlabs.io)

the Warren ledge

where you entered the Purge Core

setting.ambient_text: A subsonic hum vibrates through my bones. Amber fluid drains from my cracked pod, pooling on the organic-metallic floor. Bioluminescent veins pulse in the walls. Somewhere, something clicks. Precise, mechanical, patient.
intro_text:
You remember the Outrider's cockpit.
Earth turning blue and slow beneath you.
A routine salvage run, and a beacon in the dark
where no beacon should be.

Then the dark moved.
Something vast unfolded out of nothing — a living ship,
all tendrils and bioluminescent veins.
It swallowed the Outrider whole.

You were catalogued.
Weighed. Measured. Filed away in a pod
of warm amber fluid alongside
hundreds of other specimens.

You don't know how long you slept.
Days. Months. Years.
The ship hums around you —
a heartbeat that is not your own.

Something has gone wrong.
Your pod is cracked. The fluid is draining.
Alarms pulse in colors you have no name for.
The ship's crew is nowhere to be seen.

You are cold. You are weak.
And somewhere below this ship,
Earth is still turning.

Find a way out.

steps.text: Your cursor is your eyes and hands. Right-click to change what it does: Look (the eye), Move (the feet), Hand and Talk.
With Move (the feet), click open space to drift there. LUMEN-7's service panel is on the gold body.
Hand picks things up and works them. Take the bolt driver off the tool mount on the gold body.
What you carry is in Items. Click the bolt driver, then click the gold body to use it on the panel bolts.
Look (the eye) is always safe. Look inside the panel.
Your cursor is your eyes and hands. Right-click to change what it does: Look (the eye), Move (the feet), Hand and Talk.
With the Move cursor (the feet), click the floor to walk there.
Switch to Look (the eye) and click something to examine it. Looking is always safe.
Hand picks things up and works them. Try the specimen tag hanging from your pod.
What you carry is in Items, under the picture. Click an item, then click something in the room to use it there. Click one item and then another to combine them.
Stuck? The ? button at the bottom right gives a hint for the room you're in. Good luck.

actions.label: Listen
actions.title: Hold your breath and listen (costs a breath; you make no sound this move)

effects.text: I hold my breath and listen. Only the ship breathing. Nothing near.

kinds.label: A scorched hiss (a purge duct opens off that screen)

effects.text: I squeeze the lung-sac and breathe.

lines.text: Say again? Missing? ...Okay. Don't touch anything. I'm pulling up long-range... and long-range is acting up. Great.
Outrider, long-range is showing something. It's big. It's right on top of y—
“Control, something's pulling me in, I can't—”
Click. Click. Click. Back the way I came.
Something is standing over my empty pod.
It dips a long finger in the fluid and tilts its head. It knows something is missing.
I back away before it turns around. Quietly.

hints.text: Your pod is shattered. Search the wreckage: the broken glass and pooling fluid might be useful.
The amber fluid in the drainage channel could be useful, but you need a container. Try the other rooms: sample jars, perhaps.
You have a sample jar. Use it on the drainage channel to collect some amber stasis fluid.
There's a specimen tag on a hook by your pod, with your identification on it. Take it.
The cataloguer is across a torn gap; jumping it would be suicide. The far railing looks solid: a hook on a long, strong line might catch it.
You've gathered what you can here, and you have the cataloguer's code. The archway leads deeper into the ship.
You have part of a way across: a line won't catch and a hook won't hold. Combine them: select one item in your inventory, then click the other.
Your grappling line is ready. Select it in your inventory and use it on the gap.
You're across. Get a closer LOOK at the cataloguer robot and its specimen jars.
Your line is rigged across the pit. HAND it to climb over to the cataloguer.
Study the three specimens: Velith Ammonite, Kethrani Weaver and Neural Orchid. The screens below each tank carry alien text.
You've memorized the four characters on the specimen displays, in order. The ship's keypads use the same script.
The keypad wants four alien characters in order. Guessing would take forever: look for somewhere those characters appear in a fixed order.
You've memorized the four characters on the specimen displays, in order. The ship's keypads use the same script.
You've unlocked the terminal, and it armed the emergency override at the security console.
A specimen processing lab. The surgical instruments and data screens are worth investigating.
The instrument rack holds alien surgical tools: take one as a makeshift tool. The sample jars on the shelf might be useful too.
A sample jar on the lower shelf is empty and cracked open. You could collect liquids in it.
The data screens on the wall lead to a terminal with an alien keypad. It wants four characters in the right order.
The restraint straps held creatures far bigger than you, so they'd hold your weight. Your hands can't tear them; something made to cut this ship's materials might.
The terminal armed the emergency override at the security console. The Security Hub is off the corridor.
You've unlocked the lab terminal and opened the deck's locks. Keep exploring.
A hunter drone is guarding the terminal. Don't touch anything near it: leave the lab, and it will give up.
This corridor connects the containment sections. Explore the passages branching off in each direction.
The left passage might have tools and information. The right one could give you control over the ship's systems.
You've reached security. Straight ahead leads deeper into the ship.
You know this corridor well now. Explore every branch before looking for a way off this deck.
The override released the vent grate in the corridor floor. It leads deeper in, toward the airlock bay.
The grate is open and the hunters are out, in the rooms you came from. Go down the vent.
A grim place where the crew dispose of failed specimens. Search it: there may be something useful.
A severed neural tendril lies near a slab. Alien neural tissue could be useful elsewhere.
You've found what's useful here.
A barbed carcass hook is jammed in the lip of an open drawer. It's made to catch and hold: handy where there's a gap to cross.
The feeding station joins the morgue, the specimen archive and the corridor. Explore left and right.
The nutrient dispenser still works. The paste isn't appetizing, but it might have other uses.
The morgue is through the left passage, and the specimen archive is to the right. Both may hold items you need.
Search the morgue and the archive thoroughly. Your way off this deck is the airlock bay, beyond the ventilation shaft.
The caged creature seems to want something from you. Talk to it again: it may have more to say now.
You promised to open its cage. Whatever controls the locks on this deck might do it.
The cage is open. Look at the floor of it: the creature left something for you.
The ventilation shaft branches ahead. Someone escaped this way before you.
The scratches on the walls look deliberate. Examine them more closely.
LOOK at your map in your inventory. From the junction it's EAST, then the long way round to the north-west. The left tunnel is a dead end.
The Gut's door is far west, behind a Choir quarantine seal; the seal's lever is far east. Your map is north-up: count your turns.
The wall markings might mean something. Too bad you don't have a reference.

The map is north-up with no 'you are here': count your turns. Left is west, right is east. Go east to the lever first, then back west. The big skull is bad air (wear the helmet); small skulls are purge ducts.
These ducts all look alike. The camera always faces north: ahead is north, left west, right east. Count your turns on the map.
The Keth-Vari's scratched route says: toward the lever, go right (east) from here.

then.text: The hum behind the walls stops, then starts again, moving fast, away from you. The Curator knows where you are going. It is heading for the Purge Heart's controls to fire a purge that will clear the whole Core. Every seam brightens. It needs 5 of your moves. The Heart is 3 away.
the race to the Purge Heart

views.name: Gas-Filled Passage
views.ambient_text: Yellow-green gas swirls around me. Every breath burns.

hints.text: This section is full of toxic gas from a cracked bio-organic pipe.
The gas is lethal without protection. You need something to breathe through.
The helmet should protect you from the gas. Press forward.
A massive fan blocks the passage. Its mechanism is exposed on the wall.
The fan mechanism has an exposed gap, but you have nothing to jam it with. Did you leave a tool behind?
The fan mechanism has an exposed gap. Something long and thin, like your surgical probe, might jam the gears.
The fan is stopped. You can squeeze through the blades now.
A dead end, but not a wasted trip. The skeleton tells a story.
The skeleton is holding something that still glows faintly.
The skeleton had more than a datapad. Search the body again: check the uniform pockets.
The airlock bay is below. Drop through the hatch to reach it.
The deck's security station. The console and the drawer unit on the wall are worth a closer look.
The emergency override is dead. Something else must arm it, maybe the Processing Lab terminal.
The lab terminal armed the emergency override. Look closely at the console and press it.
The drawer unit on the wall is jammed half-open, and there are key cards inside.
You have the key card and the locks are open. The vent in the corridor floor leads to the airlock bay.
The emergency override button is the control that matters here.
The override button is dead. Something has to arm it: the Processing Lab terminal is on the same network.
The override is armed. Press the red button.
The deck's locks are open, including the vent grate in the corridor floor.
Once the alarm goes, you can't come back for things. The air in the deep ducts isn't safe. Is there anything on this deck to breathe through?
Once the alarm goes, you can't come back for things. Something in the ducts spins very fast; a thin, strong tool from the lab might stop it.
Once the alarm goes, you can't come back for things. Doors beyond the ducts will want a key card, and there's one on this deck.
The archive holds the Choir's records of every species they've collected. The data crystals and reading device are worth a look.
One data crystal is out of place, a personal log perhaps. Take it and use it on the reading device.
You have the data crystal. Insert it into the reading device to decrypt it.
The holographic display shows the Convergence's path of destruction. Examine it to see what you're up against.
You've uncovered the Choir's records and the Convergence's history. It will matter deeper in.
An airlock bay. Look around: the clamps, the viewport, the override panel.
The docking clamps are empty: your ship is gone. Check the suit locker and the viewport.
The viewport shutters answer to a key card. Have a look outside.
The override panel is locked. You need a containment key card; try the Security Hub.
You have the containment key card. Use it on the override panel to unlock the airlock systems.
The override panel is open. You've escaped the containment deck: this is as far as Act 1 goes.
The bridge holds the ship's star charts and navigation systems. Understanding where this vessel has been could reveal where it's going.
The star map shows the Convergence's path. The command console may have a removable navigation chip with jump coordinates.
You have the navigation data. Engineering and the comm array are accessible from here.
The ship's reactor pulses like a living heart. Look for portable power sources and coolant — both could be invaluable.
The reactor access panel might yield a power cell. The coolant system could provide a useful chemical agent.
You've salvaged what you can from engineering. The shuttle bay and waste processing are accessible from here.
The communications array handles all signals to and from The Convergence. The schematics and recording station may hold useful intelligence.
Look for the comm array schematics — understanding the frequencies could let you send your own transmissions later.
You have the schematics. The data core and navigation bridge are connected from here.
The Choir's weapons are biometrically locked, but something has already been removed from one rack. Search for anything you can actually use.
The resonance disruptor on the workbench might be operable. It disrupts bio-mechanical systems — extremely useful against Choir technology.
The resonance disruptor is yours. The hive quarters and shuttle bay connect from here.
The Choir's living quarters. Their resonance chamber and dormancy alcoves might hold items attuned to their biology.
The resonance chamber could contain a Choir crystal — their communication medium. A cipher fragment may be hidden in their patterns.
You've gathered what you can from the Choir's quarters. The armory, comm array, and waste processing are accessible from here.
A damaged shuttle sits in the bay. It might be your ticket off this ship — if you can repair it.
The shuttle needs fuel, power, and navigation to fly. Look for a fuel line in the supply rack, and bring a power cell and navigation chip from elsewhere.
You have what you need to start repairs. Install the fuel line, power cell, and navigation chip into the shuttle systems.
The ship's bio-garden grows alien plants. Some may have biochemical properties worth harvesting.
The harvest station has concentrated bio-extract, and the fiber plants produce incredibly strong strands. Take both.
You've harvested what you need. These materials can be combined with other items for new tools.
The ship's data core — an organic brain that stores all operational data. The interface terminal may let you access encrypted Convergence communications.
Use the interface terminal to query the organic brain. The Convergence's encrypted communications could reveal their plans for this planet.
You've accessed the data core. The comm array and hydroponics connect from here.
The ship's waste processing. Catwalks over grinding machinery. A dangerous place, but perhaps something useful was discarded here.
A disabled maintenance drone near the catwalks still has its sensory antenna intact. It could detect Choir patrol signals.
You've taken the drone antenna. Engineering and the hive quarters are accessible from here.
The observation deck offers a view of the planet below. The instruments here monitor the harvesting process.
Study the observation instruments carefully. Understanding the energy siphon network could be critical when you reach the surface.
You've studied the siphon network. The bridge and hydroponics connect from here.
You've crashed on the planet's surface. Search the wreckage for anything salvageable before moving on.
The shuttle interior may have an emergency beacon and other supplies. The wasteland stretches out beyond the crash site.
You've salvaged what you can. Head into the wasteland to find the planet's former inhabitants and their weapons.
The shuttle's interior is smashed but some systems still function. Check the dashboard, emergency kit, and personal storage.
The emergency beacon and signal flare could save your life. Take everything that isn't bolted down.
You've taken everything useful from the wreck.
The wasteland stretches in all directions. Paths lead to a siphon tower, a refugee camp, a fungal grove, and an overlook.
The siphon tower has energy crystals worth collecting. The refugee camp might have supplies and information from the former inhabitants.
The city gates lie beyond the echo field near the refugee camp. You'll need to prepare before venturing there.
A massive energy siphon tower drains life from the planet. The crystals at its base pulse with raw Convergence energy.
Break off a siphon crystal fragment and take a mineral sample. Both contain Convergence energy that could be weaponized.
You've collected what you need from the tower. These materials can be combined with items from the ship.
The remains of a refugee camp. The former inhabitants fled here before the end. Search their belongings for supplies and information.
A journal among the scattered belongings could contain a cipher fragment. The supply crate may still have rations and climbing gear.
You've gathered what the refugees left behind. The echo field beyond could lead to the city.
Bioluminescent fungi thrive here, feeding on the Convergence's residual energy. Their biochemistry could be potent.
Extract the concentrated fungal compounds. They could be combined with other chemicals for powerful effects.
You have the extract. A buried military bunker is accessible deeper in the grove.
Reality warps here — echoes of the dead civilization manifest as ghostly apparitions. Navigate carefully.
The echo stabilizer from the bunker could help you pass through safely. Without it, the echo field is dangerous and disorienting.
The city gates are visible through the distortion. Press on toward the dead civilization's last stronghold.
A military bunker from the planet's final days. The door may require a code. Search for one among the refugee camp's belongings.
The bunker holds military equipment — an echo stabilizer, weapons, defense schematics, and a radiation badge. Take everything.
You've taken everything useful from the bunker. The echo stabilizer will help you navigate the echo field toward the city.
The gates of the dead city loom before you. They may need a keystone or a specific approach to open.
The gates are open. The dead city awaits. The overlook nearby offers a panoramic view of what lies ahead.
From this vantage point you can see the dead city spread below, the siphon towers draining it, and the nexus at its heart.
The panoramic vista reveals the layout of the city. Study it — knowledge of the terrain will help you navigate below.
The grand plaza of a dead civilization. Explore the buildings, monuments, and pathways branching from here.
The central statue may hold a keystone — an access token for restricted areas. The map kiosk could reveal the city's layout.
You have the keystone and know the layout. The library, war room, and research lab hold the information you need to find the weapon.
The city's library — a vast collection of crystalline knowledge. The translation cipher will help you read the ancient texts.
Search the crystal stacks for the final cipher fragment. The reading station and holographic index can help decipher the planet's history.
With the cipher fragments, you can assemble a complete translation. Use it to read the Convergence section for weapon intelligence.
The military command center. The holographic table and tactical displays show the civilization's last stand against the Convergence.
The defense grid controller on the tactical table could control orbital defense satellites — if any still function.
You have the controller. The battle plans mention a countermeasure weapon — its schematics may be in the research lab.
The research lab where the countermeasure weapon was designed. The prototype and schematics are here.
Study the prototype weapon and find the assembly blueprint. You'll need to understand exactly how to build the countermeasure.
You have the blueprint and know the weapon design. The lab goggles will protect you from dangerous energy when you reach the nexus.
Homes abandoned in haste. The packed luggage and half-eaten meals paint a picture of sudden evacuation.
A personal locket among the possessions might hold emotional significance. An echo of a former resident may appear if you're still enough.
You've seen the lives that were lived here. Their memory drives you forward.
The city's power station. The reactor is offline but the backup systems might be restorable.
Restart the reactor to power the city's systems. The power distribution panel and adapter will let you bridge alien technology together.
Power is restored. The city's transit system and other infrastructure should be functional now.
A sacred place. The resonance chamber and altar held spiritual significance for the former inhabitants.
The prophet's crystal on the altar shows visions of possible futures. The resonance tuning fork could communicate with echoes.
You have the crystal and tuning fork. These sacred tools may prove decisive at the nexus.
The city's underground transit. The rails lead deeper — toward the weapon vault and the nexus beyond.
The railway controls need a pass token and power to function. Check the platform area for a token.
You have the pass token. With city power restored, the railway can take you deeper.
Reality splits here — one half pristine, one half ruined. A ghost scientist lingers at the boundary.
The echo communicator could let you speak with the ghost scientist. They may know the vault's access codes.
The scientist's echo has shared what it knows. The weapon vault should be accessible now.
The weapon vault — where the countermeasure was stored. Security systems still guard the weapon core.
The biometric lock requires ancient access authorization. The vault's energy barriers and security door must be bypassed.
The weapon core sits on its pedestal. Take it — this is what the entire civilization built to fight the Convergence.
The ground crystallizes beneath your feet. The nexus is close — reality itself bends around the Convergence's power.
Press forward. The entrance to the nexus lies ahead. Prepare everything you have — there may be no turning back.
The nexus gate pulses with Convergence energy. Ancient markings from the former inhabitants surround the entrance.
Study the ancient markings — they may reveal how the former civilization intended to approach the nexus. The descent tunnel leads down.
Rivers of raw energy flow through massive conduits. A narrow metal walkway spans the chasm.
The shielded helmet will protect you from the energy. Cross the walkway to reach the convergence chamber. An energy sample point could yield pure Convergence energy.
The heart of the harvesting apparatus. A beam of energy connects the planet's core to the ship above. This is where it all ends — or begins.
The countermeasure slot at the base of the apparatus is where the weapon must be deployed. Assemble the countermeasure from the weapon core and your gathered components.
The assembled countermeasure is ready. Place it in the slot to end the harvesting — but consider your options. There may be other ways to resolve this.
The control spire oversees the entire harvesting operation. Choir consoles and ancient controls coexist here.
The spire interface module could let you communicate directly with the Convergence. The ancient controls might offer alternative solutions.
A gallery of the Convergence's oldest specimens — civilizations consumed across eons. A pedestal holds an ancient access key.
Take the ancient access key from the pedestal. It opens the deepest sections of the nexus.
A staging area where the former inhabitants prepared their assault on the nexus. The workbench can assemble complex devices.
Use the assembly workbench to combine the weapon core with your gathered components. The blueprint shows the full recipe.
The countermeasure is assembled. Take it to the convergence chamber to deploy it.
A crystal antenna array capable of broadcasting across the galaxy. The consoles control targeting and frequency.
With the comm schematics and a galactic broadcast assembled, you could warn other civilizations about the Convergence.
The Convergence itself. An ancient intelligence, vast and patient, that has consumed worlds for longer than most stars have burned.
The core interface point allows direct neural contact with the Convergence. You could confront it, reason with it, or merge with it. Choose carefully — this decides everything.
A vertical shaft carved by the former inhabitants as an emergency exit. It leads to the surface — and freedom, if you can reach it.
The shaft gate requires a key. The carved ladder leads up, but a collapsed section blocks the way. The climbing pitons could help.
The shaft is open. Climb toward the light above — but are you sure you've done everything you needed to?
Take it in. Then click anywhere.

views.name: LUMEN-7, High Orbit
views.ambient_text: Four hundred kilometres up. The only sound is your own breathing, and LUMEN-7 saying nothing at all.

effects.text: Outrider, Relay. Still nothing from LUMEN on our end. Tell me you've got eyes on it.
“Eyes on it. Big, expensive, and not talking. Heading for the access panel.”

hints.text: LUMEN-7's service panel is on the gold body, bolted shut. Take the bolt driver off the tool mount with Hand, then click it in Items and click the gold body.
You have the bolt driver. Click it in Items, then click LUMEN-7's gold body to take the bolts out.

views.name: LUMEN-7 Service Panel
views.ambient_text: LUMEN-7's service panel, open. Your breath fogs the bottom of your visor.

hints.text: LOOK inside the panel.

items.name: Empty Sample Jar
items.description: A small bio-organic jar from the processing lab, now empty. Good for liquid samples.

then.text: A little jar of ship-stuff, seal broken but intact. It could hold a few ounces of liquid.
Lighter than glass and slightly warm. It still smells of formaldehyde, or the alien equivalent.

items.name: Stasis Fluid Vial
items.description: A vial of amber stasis fluid from my broken pod, still faintly shimmering.

then.text: Warm, thick, faintly glowing amber. It kept me and hundreds of others under. Alien, but built to keep things alive.
I swirl it. It moves like honey and clings to the glass.

items.name: Pod Glass Shard
items.description: A curved shard from my broken stasis pod. Sharp enough to cut.

then.text: Translucent, curved, stained amber, razor-edged. Some composite stronger and lighter than glass.
I test the edge on my thumb. Blood, immediately. Careful with this.

items.name: Surgical Probe
items.description: An alien surgical instrument: curved, bone-like, with a fine tip.

then.text: Grown, not made: smooth bone tapering to a needle point. The grip's made for longer fingers, but it'll do.

items.name: Containment Key Card
items.description: A bio-organic access card from the security hub. Pulses faintly.

then.text: Something like compressed cartilage laced with glowing circuits, pulsing like a heartbeat. Keyed to containment deck security.

items.name: Data Crystal — Personal Log
items.description: A small data crystal from the specimen archive: a Choir officer's personal records.

then.text: Thumb-sized and faceted, its light shifting as I tilt it. A Choir personal log, holding a fragment of a translation cipher. Piece one of four.

items.name: Nutrient Paste Tube
items.description: A tube of grey nutrient slurry from the feeding station. Smells like wet cardboard and pennies.

then.text: Specimen feed, nutritionally complete for a dozen species and appetising to none. It could be bait: the drones are programmed to retrieve spilled feed.

items.name: Specimen Tag
items.description: My own specimen tag from the stasis pod. Proof of what I am to them.

then.text: On the back, a ring of seven marks, six of them dark. A countdown, and I'm the last mark. I'd rather not see it go out.

items.name: Emergency Suit Helmet
items.description: An alien emergency helmet. Too big for me, but it works.

then.text: Made for a Choir skull, so it sits on me like a fishbowl, but the visor seals and the air system works. Good against vacuum and toxic air.

items.name: Ventilation Map
items.description: The escapee's map of the vents, scratched on a metal plate, north at the top. The Gut's east half is torn off. Look at it to read it.

then.text: North at the top: the Outer Ducts along the bottom, the Gut in the middle (east half torn off), the Purge Core on top. Circles are cold folds, rings breathing ducts, skulls purge ducts, bars grates. Nothing marks where I am.

items.name: Severed Neural Tendril
items.description: A length of neural interface tendril, cut from an alien dormancy alcove.

then.text: Rubbery, a foot long, the cut end still sparking. The Choir plug these into their ship. With the right adapter, maybe I could too, if it can be fooled into taking human biology.

items.name: Ship's Black Box
items.description: The Choir vessel's flight recorder: the full mission log, including every world consumed.

then.text: Dense and heavily shielded: navigation logs, mission orders, specimen records, messages with the Convergence. Proof of what they've done, and what they're doing to the planet below.

items.name: Power Cell
items.description: A Choir power cell from engineering. Small, immensely powerful, warm.

then.text: A dense energy core in a bio-organic casing, humming and warm. One runs a Choir shuttle for weeks. Crack the casing and it lets go violently.

items.name: Resonance Disruptor
items.description: A Choir tool turned weapon. Its subsonic pulse disrupts bio-mechanical systems.

then.text: A maintenance tool, really. Aimed at a bio-organic lock, it scrambles the resonance; aimed at a drone, it stalls it for a few seconds. Closest thing to a universal key.

items.name: Navigation Chip
items.description: A crystal navigation module from the bridge: star charts and jump coordinates.

then.text: A slim crystal wafer: star charts, jump coordinates, the Convergence's path across galaxies. Without it, no ship leaves this system; the jumps are too complex to work out by hand.

items.name: Translation Cipher Fragment 2
items.description: A data pattern from the Choir's resonance chamber. The second piece of the translation key.

then.text: Taken from the resonance patterns in the Choir's quarters. Their language is subsonic vibration, and this maps vibrations to meaning. With the other fragments, I could read their text.

items.name: Choir Resonance Crystal
items.description: A data-core crystal that resonates at the Choir's communication frequency.

then.text: Deep purple, perfectly smooth, humming at a pitch I feel in my teeth. Tuned to the Choir's network, the same frequency the Convergence uses to control its harvesters.

items.name: Bio-Garden Extract
items.description: A glowing, chemically complex extract from the ship's hydroponics bay.

then.text: From the bio-garden's plants, glowing blue-green and dense with compounds. The Choir use it for food and neural repair. Combined right, it could bridge organic and crystalline systems.

items.name: Comm Array Schematics
items.description: Diagrams of the ship's communication array: frequencies, power and range.

then.text: Frequencies, power routing, targeting. With these, the array at the planet's nexus could be retuned to broadcast across the galaxy, if I could reach it.

items.name: Shuttle Fuel Line
items.description: A replacement fuel line for the damaged shuttle: organic tubing with self-sealing connectors.

then.text: Bio-organic tubing whose connectors seal when pressed home. This, plus a power cell, gets the damaged shuttle flying.

items.name: Drone Antenna
items.description: A sensory antenna from a disabled maintenance drone. Still picks up Choir signals.

then.text: Thin, segmented, twitching. Held to my ear, it picks up the Choir's distant clicks and hums. An early warning system.

items.name: Coolant Flask
items.description: A sealed flask of reactor coolant from engineering. Extremely cold, mildly corrosive.

then.text: Frosted over; the coolant is near absolute zero. Crack the seal and out comes freezing vapour. For overheated systems, or anything organic in a pinch.

items.name: Bio-Garden Fiber
items.description: Strong, flexible fibre from alien plants. Tougher than any rope.

then.text: From the hydroponics tendrils; the Choir build and repair with it. It weaves, ties and wraps. With something sharp, it'd make a fine handle or binding.

items.name: Shuttle Emergency Beacon
items.description: A distress beacon from the crashed shuttle. Recalls any shuttle in range.

then.text: A transmitter that calls a shuttle to it, with range across the whole planet. If there's a working shuttle anywhere, this brings it. My ticket off this rock, if I want it.

items.name: Wasteland Mineral Sample
items.description: A mineral crystal from the base of a siphon tower, holding Convergence energy.

then.text: Soil by the siphon towers, crystallised by the extraction. It holds a faint charge, and it resists energy flow rather than conducting it.

items.name: Siphon Crystal Fragment
items.description: A fragment broken off an energy siphon tower. Pulses with raw Convergence energy.

then.text: It burns cold and crackles, still full of stolen planetary life. Very dangerous. Key to anything that has to touch Convergence energy systems.

items.name: Refugee Journal
items.description: A journal from the refugee camp, written by a four-armed scientist in the final days.

then.text: Dr. Kaelith's journal, a physicist who fled the city when the siphons began: the panic, the failed defences, the late evacuation. In the margins, cipher notation. Fragment three of four.

items.name: Fungal Extract
items.description: An extract of the grove's glowing fungi. Purple in the dark.

then.text: The fungi feed on the Convergence's leftover energy instead of being drained. The extract heals tissue and, with the right compounds, can suppress neural detection.

items.name: Echo Stabilizer
items.description: Military tech from the bunker. Stabilises the field around Echoes so they're safe to approach.

then.text: A handheld stabilising field, built to study the Echoes: people trapped in the Convergence's energy. It calms them enough to interact with. Without it, getting near one is like standing in a lightning storm.

items.name: Alien Sidearm
items.description: A four-armed species' sidearm. Energy-based, partly charged.

then.text: Made for a four-armed grip; I need both hands. Maybe six shots left, each one deafening. Use it wisely, or not at all.

items.name: Bunker Defense Schematics
items.description: Military blueprints of the planet's defence against the Convergence.

then.text: Plans for a last stand: orbital defence satellites, ground weapons, and partial schematics of a weapon to disrupt the Convergence's energy. Incomplete, but they prove it was built.

items.name: Survival Rations
items.description: Preserved alien food from the refugee camp. Still sealed, still edible.

then.text: Vacuum-packed rations; the label shows a happy four-armed diner. Close enough for me. Eating one restores energy and clears my head.

items.name: Signal Flare
items.description: An emergency signal flare from the Outrider's kit. Burns bright, burns loud.

then.text: From the Outrider's emergency kit. Pull the cap and it burns blinding white for thirty seconds: a signal, a light, a distraction, or, wrapped right, a torch.

items.name: Climbing Pitons
items.description: Metal spikes from the refugee camp's supplies, for climbing rock.

then.text: Hardened spikes with loops for rope; the refugees climbed the wasteland with them. For anything I can't reach on my own.

items.name: Radiation Badge
items.description: A sensor badge from the bunker. Changes colour near dangerous Convergence energy.

then.text: A crystal strip: green safe, yellow caution, red lethal. Soldiers used them near siphon towers. Near the nexus, it'll show the safe paths.

items.name: City Keystone
items.description: An ornamental keystone from the plaza's central statue. Opens restricted areas in the city.

then.text: A crystal key shaped like a tiny four-armed figure: an administrator's master key, once set in the plaza statue. It opens government buildings, the war room and restricted infrastructure.

items.name: Translation Cipher Fragment 4
items.description: The last fragment of the translation cipher, from the city library.

then.text: The last cipher fragment, from the library's master index: the city's key for its failed talks with the Choir. With all four, I can read any alien inscription.

items.name: Weapon Core
items.description: The heart of the city's countermeasure weapon: a dense crystal sphere with energy pulsing inside.

then.text: Like holding a small star. It resonates at the Convergence's own frequency, to turn its stolen energy on it. Inert alone; with the right parts, it can destroy the nexus.

items.name: Defense Grid Controller
items.description: A command module for the planet's orbital defense satellites.

then.text: Most of its satellites are gone, but a few sleep in orbit. With enough power, they could make one devastating strike.

items.name: Alien Personal Locket
items.description: A delicate locket from a family home, with a holographic portrait inside.

then.text: A four-armed family of five, all smiling; the youngest holds a toy siphon tower. Carried near coherent Echoes, it sets off powerful reactions.

items.name: Power Cell Adapter
items.description: An adapter that bridges this planet's technology with alien power sources.

then.text: Built to run the city's crystal systems off captured Choir power cells. A universal translator for machines.

items.name: Prophet's Crystal
items.description: A sacred crystal from the temple. It shows possible futures to whoever holds it.

then.text: The priests divined with these, and beat the odds. I see flashes: a nexus in flames, a signal to the stars, a frightened crystal mind, a small creature choosing.

items.name: Railway Pass Token
items.description: An access token for the city's underground railway.

then.text: A crystal pass that starts the city's rail cars, where the railway still has power. The tunnels also reach deeper passages under the city.

items.name: Resonance Tuning Fork
items.description: A temple tuning fork. It hums at the old civilization's speaking frequency.

then.text: They spoke by vibration. Combined with the Echo Stabilizer, this fork could let me truly talk with coherent Echoes.

items.name: Lab Safety Goggles
items.description: Research-lab goggles that filter dangerous energy wavelengths.

then.text: Too big for my face, but they filter the blinding light of Convergence systems, so I can look at high-energy areas and keep my eyes.

items.name: Ancient Blueprint
items.description: Assembly instructions for the countermeasure weapon, from the research lab.

then.text: Three parts: a primed weapon core, an energy dampener and a siphon crystal fragment. Order matters: core first, dampener second, crystal last.

items.name: Convergence Energy Sample
items.description: Pure Convergence energy in a crystal vial. Incredibly dangerous.

then.text: Cold enough to burn, bright enough to read by: a world's harvested life force. The vial barely holds it.

items.name: Ancient Access Key
items.description: A key from the Convergence's stasis gallery. It opens the deepest parts of the nexus.

then.text: Older than the Choir and this planet both: a crystal fractal that fits the oldest locks in the nexus.

items.name: Curator's Signal Device
items.description: The Curator's own signal device. It can call the Choir vessel from orbit.

then.text: Keyed to the Curator's authority: it can recall the ship, command drones and override security.

items.name: Core Interface Module
items.description: A control-spire module for a direct neural link with the Convergence intelligence.

then.text: The Choir take orders from the Convergence through these. Prepared right, any mind could link to it. Coming back is another matter.

items.name: Escape Shaft Key
items.description: A mechanical key to the old civilization's emergency escape shaft in the nexus.

then.text: It opens the shaft the old civilization carved up to the surface. My way out, if I take it.

items.name: Charged Sidearm
items.description: The four-armed sidearm, fully charged with a Choir power cell.

then.text: Twenty shots instead of six. The grip was made for more hands than I have.

items.name: Complete Translation Cipher
items.description: The complete translation cipher: all four fragments joined.

then.text: Every alien inscription is readable now. I used to struggle with flight-manual French.

items.name: Countermeasure Stage2
items.description: The primed core inside its energy dampener.

then.text: One part left: the siphon crystal fragment.

items.name: Echo Communicator
items.description: The Echo Stabilizer with the temple tuning fork mounted in its emitter.

then.text: It carries my words to Echoes and brings their answers back clear.

items.name: Energy Dampener
items.description: A palm-sized blob of gel that drinks energy.

then.text: It soaks up power on contact and makes a dead zone near Convergence systems.

items.name: Improvised Torch
items.description: A flare wrapped in bio-fiber: a slow, steady torch.

then.text: It burns steady instead of blinding, and lasts far longer than the flare.

items.name: Neural Suppressant
items.description: A paste that hides neural signatures.

then.text: Smeared on skin, it hides me from anything that senses energy, Echoes included. It smells as good as it sounds.

items.name: Orbital Weapon
items.description: The defense grid controller, wired to the overcharge device.

then.text: Power for one devastating strike: the nexus, or the Choir ship.

items.name: Overcharge Device
items.description: A disruptor pulse amplified through a siphon crystal.

then.text: It can overload any energy system I aim it at. Once.

items.name: Partial Cipher 12
items.description: Two cipher fragments, interlocked: half the translation key.

then.text: Enough for simple alien text. Two fragments to go.

items.name: Partial Cipher 123
items.description: Three cipher fragments joined: most of the translation key.

then.text: I can read most operational text now. One fragment remains.

items.name: Primed Weapon Core
items.description: The weapon core, tuned with a Choir crystal and humming.

then.text: It hums at the Convergence's frequency. Next: the dampener, then the siphon crystal fragment.

items.name: Reinforced Blade
items.description: The glass shard with a bio-fiber grip: a proper blade.

then.text: Stronger than tape. I can hold it without cutting myself, which is new.

items.name: Sedative Compound
items.description: Nutrient paste soaked in stasis fluid, now a deep amber.

then.text: The stuff that kept me asleep for days, concentrated. Touch it and sleep.

items.name: Shielded Helmet
items.description: The helmet, lined with energy dampener gel.

then.text: With this on, the nexus's high-energy chambers won't fry my nerves.

items.name: The Countermeasure
items.description: The complete countermeasure weapon.

then.text: It hums with the Convergence's own stolen energy. It kills planets. It can save them too.

items.name: Universal Bypass
items.description: The key card, rewritten by the disruptor: every access level at once.

then.text: It claims every clearance at once, and the doors seem to believe it.

items.name: Universal Interface
items.description: The power adapter married to the navigation chip: a skeleton key for machines.

then.text: It can talk to anything: Choir, Convergence, or the old civilization's systems.

items.name: Galactic Broadcast
items.description: A recorded broadcast signal, ready to transmit to the galaxy.

then.text: Evidence of the harvest in one signal. Sent, it could warn every world in range.

items.name: Neural Bridge
items.description: A device that links two minds directly.

then.text: An alien neural bridge. It could open a direct link to the Nexus consciousness.

items.name: Choir Crew Datapad
items.description: A Choir datapad from a dead crew member in the vents. Still faintly glowing.

then.text: A Choir crewman's last log: a breach, the Curator sweeping the decks (crew too), a dash for the airlock through the vents. The last entry: coordinates, the ship's orbit over a blue world, and an override frequency for the operational decks.

items.name: Choir Access Chip
items.description: A small crystal security chip from a dead Choir crewman's uniform, still keyed to his clearance.

examine.response: Veined with light, it broadcasts the holder's clearance to Choir locks, and the dead engineer's is still stored. It might fool a few doors.
The chip pulses faster in my palm, trying to read me. Wrong species, but the stored clearance may still open Choir systems.

items.name: Restraint Strap
items.description: A long restraint strap cut from a processing-lab table. Tougher than any rope.

then.text: Thick, leathery and warm, strong enough to hold many times my weight. On its own, there's nothing to anchor it with.

items.name: Carcass Hook
items.description: A barbed bio-metal hook from the morgue, for dragging bodies out of drawers.

then.text: Curved like a talon, with a backward barb and a thick eyelet. It would bite into any edge. Shame there's nothing tied to it.

items.name: Grappling Line
items.description: A carcass hook knotted to a length of restraint strap. Crude, but it will hold.

then.text: The strap cinched through the hook's eyelet with the best knot I know. Throw it, let the barb bite, and it'll take my weight.

items.name: Wedding Ring
items.description: A plain gold band from the dead man in the morgue.

then.text: Engraved inside, worn almost smooth: 'M & J. Always.' No use to me at all, and the most human thing on this ship.

items.name: Lung-sac
items.description: A living air bladder from the Queen. It holds four breaths and refills at folds and air rooms.

then.text: A plump amber-veined sac tied off with sinew. It holds four breaths: squeeze it (the button up top) to breathe anywhere. Folds and air rooms refill it.
I squeeze the lung-sac and breathe what it gives me.

items.name: Call-stone
items.description: A hollow shell with breathing holes. Tap it on a grate and the colony knocks on the walls far away.

then.text: Tapped on a grate in the Core, it sets the colony knocking far off and draws the Curator away. Two taps; they come back if I start the Core again.

items.name: Hollowed Tag
items.description: My specimen tag, eaten hollow by the brood. The Choir have lost my trail.

then.text: Riddled with bore holes, its display dark. The brood ate the signal and the countdown with it. It still says what I am, just not where.

items.name: The Queen's Egg
items.description: One of the colony's eggs, in a cradle of sinew. A gift for someone she calls kin.

then.text: A hen's-egg-sized sac of glowing amber with a curled larva inside. It's warm, and now and then it breathes.

items.name: Claw Ring
items.description: A curved Keth-Vari claw bound into a ring with copper wire.

then.text: One of the Keth-Vari's own claws, wired into a loop and scratched with tally marks. It fits. A promise in a language I'm still learning.

items.name: Vera's Patch
items.description: Vera Halloran's mission patch, torn from her flight suit. Her name, to take home.

then.text: Faded orange, a rocket in a ring of stars. On the back in marker: V. HALLORAN, LIFE SUPPORT. I'll take her name home.

items.name: Choir Multitool
items.description: A Choir maintenance tool, long and strong. It would jam almost anything.

then.text: From the Cache: a long bone-handled rod with a dozen folding prongs. Long and strong enough to jam a fan.

items.name: Bolt Driver
items.description: A cordless bolt driver on a tether clip.

then.text: The tool mount's empty now. The driver's with me.

combinations.message: I thread the strap through the hook's eyelet, cinch it and haul with all my weight. It holds: a grappling line.
I wrap the bio-fiber around the base of the glass shard. It bonds to the glass, stronger than tape. A proper blade now.
Paste and stasis fluid turn deep amber: the stuff that kept me asleep for days, smearable. Touch it and sleep.
I pulse the disruptor through the key card's bio-circuits. It now claims every access level at once.
The mineral sets in the stasis fluid into a gel that drinks power on contact: a dead zone near Convergence systems.
The siphon crystal amplifies the disruptor a hundredfold: one burst that can overload any energy system. One shot.
Fungal extract and sedative make a paste that hides me from anything that senses energy, Echoes included.
The two fragments interlock: half the cipher. Simple alien text only, for now. Two fragments to go.
The journal's margin notes add a third fragment. I can read most operational text now. One remains.
The last fragment locks in, and every inscription, label and record is readable. Like remembering a language I forgot.
I press the Choir crystal to the weapon core and it hums at the Convergence's frequency. Primed. Next: the dampener, then the siphon crystal fragment.
The adapter bridges the navigation chip to a universal power bus: a skeleton key for any machine.
I wire the overcharge device into the defense grid controller: power for one strike, at the nexus or the Choir ship.
Bio-fiber around the flare's head: it burns slow and steady, a torch that far outlasts the flare.
I line the helmet with dampener gel. Now the nexus's high-energy chambers won't fry my nerves.
With the tuning fork in its emitter, the stabilizer carries my words to Echoes and brings their answers back clear.
The Choir power cell slots in and the sidearm hums. Twenty shots instead of six. The four-armed grip is awkward.
The dampener wraps the primed core. One more part, the siphon crystal fragment, and the countermeasure is done.
The siphon crystal fragment snaps in, and the countermeasure wakes, humming with stolen energy. It kills planets. It can save them too.

objects.name: Shadow Cat
objects.description: A small black cat with glowing purple-amber eyes. Nothing like it belongs on an alien harvester.

interactions.response: A black cat watches me with purple-amber eyes, its fur faintly shimmering like starlight. How did it get here?
I whisper to the cat. It blinks slowly, twice, deciding whether I'm worth its time.

then.text: The cat pushes into my palm and leans on my shin, purring like a small engine. Then it trots off, tail up, and looks back once, as if to make sure I'll remember it.

interactions.response: The cat is gone. Cats are like that.
I grab for the cat. Better men have tried. It's gone before my hand arrives.

objects.name: Your Broken Pod
objects.description: The pod I woke in. Cracked glass, amber fluid pooling beneath.

then.text: I climb back into my pod, knees up, and go limp: just another specimen. Hold still.
I curl up in my pod. The clicking passes along the walkway, hesitates, and fades.
The pod hangs open and drained, my outline pressed into the residue, arms crossed like a pharaoh. A specimen tag dangles from the frame.
I snap a curved shard off the broken edge: some alien composite, light and razor-sharp. A crude tool, but a tool.
"How long was I in there?" The pod answers with a drip.
I give the pod a shove. It's fused to the wall, which is more than can be said for my nerves.

objects.name: Drainage Channel
objects.description: A channel beneath the pods where spilled stasis fluid collects.

then.text: A shallow floor channel draining slowly to the ship's recyclers. Amber stasis fluid pools here.
The fluid is too thick to scoop and slips through my fingers. I need a container; the processing lab down the corridor might have one.
The channel is mostly drained now. Just an amber film, nothing worth collecting.
I dip the jar into the amber fluid. It fills fast and seals itself with a soft click.
The fluid gurgles into the drain in a slow pulse, like breathing.
It's a channel in the floor. I can't pick up a channel. I checked.

objects.name: Occupied Stasis Pods
objects.description: Rows of intact pods rising into the shadows. A few still glow.

then.text: Pods climb into the dark, specimens from dozens of worlds in amber. A few still pulse with life. All too high to reach.

interactions.response: I tap the nearest pod. The fluid swirls; the creature inside doesn't stir.

then.text: "Can you hear me?" The creature inside doesn't stir. Maybe that's a mercy.

objects.name: Specimen Tag
objects.description: A small tag hanging from my pod's frame, etched with alien notation.

then.text: A bio-organic tag like a leaf of cartilage, etched with alien notation. A serial number for a collected specimen. Me.
I snap the tag free. On the back, seven alien marks in a ring, six already dark. I don't need a translator to read a countdown. I pocket it anyway.
I try mouthing the alien numerals on the tag. Human throats weren't built for this.
The hook bends a little, then springs back. It's had a lot of practice holding on to things.

objects.name: Examination Tables
objects.description: Long tables with organic restraints, made for specimens much bigger than me.

then.text: Two examination tables, their organic clamps sized for things far larger than a man. They've seen a lot of use.
I touch the restraints and they twitch, sensing a meal of biomass. I step back quickly.
I put my shoulder to the table. The table, which weighs about as much as a car, does not notice.
"Whatever they did here, they did it to a lot of us."

objects.name: Surgical Instrument Rack
objects.description: A rack of alien surgical tools: curved bone-like instruments, probes and extractors.

then.text: Grown surgical tools, laid out with obsessive care. Most are made for bigger hands than mine, but a small probe near the bottom looks manageable.
I take the smallest probe, fine-tipped and flexible. Good for locks, screws and delicate mechanisms.
I give the rack a tug. It tugs back. I stop.
None of these tools match any surgery I know, which is not reassuring.

objects.name: Sample Jars
objects.description: Shelves of preserved biological samples in sealed jars.

then.text: Sealed jars of tissue and organs. I spot a heart and an eye and stop looking. One jar on the lower shelf is empty, its seal cracked open.
Sealed jars of tissue and organs. I spot a heart and an eye and stop looking.
One jar on the lower shelf is cracked open, its contents dried to a crust. I pry it free. The jar itself is intact: good for collecting samples.
I reach toward the jars and pull back. Their contents shift when my shadow falls on them.
The jars are grown into their recesses. Also, I'd really rather not hold one.
I whisper to the nearest jar. The pale thing inside twitches. I stop whispering.

objects.name: Lab Data Screens
objects.description: Screens cycling through biological data and procedures.

interactions.response: Not with the hunter drone hanging right beside it. I'll leave the lab and come back when it's gone.

then.text: I reach for the terminal. The drone's lens snaps onto me.

then.title: Caught
then.reason: The drone was waiting for exactly that. It pins you to the terminal until the Curator arrives. Next time, leave the lab and let it lose interest.

then.text: The screens cycle through intake, classification, preservation, disposal. Below them, a terminal with an alien keypad. I lean in...
I step up to the screens and the terminal beneath them...
I'd sooner try to move a patch of skin. Which, to be fair, is roughly what this is.
"Hello?" A symbol flickers politely. I feel like I've just tried French on a fax machine.

objects.name: Main Display
objects.description: A large green screen showing an alien organism diagram with alien annotations.

then.text: A spiny, many-limbed organism drawn in green lines, framed by curling alien script. The screen is locked to this display.

The screen cycles processing schedules. The current harvest: one yellow star, eight planets, the third from the sun. Earth. The ship is already in orbit. Red script at the bottom: the security console's override is armed.
Earth is still on the harvesting schedule. I have to stop this ship, or warn someone. Red script at the bottom: the security console's override is armed.
The screen ripples like warm, wet skin. Living tissue, not a monitor.

interactions.response: I ask the screen nicely. It continues not to speak English.

objects.name: Alien Keypad
objects.description: A small keypad with alien characters etched into bio-organic keys.

then.text: Eight bio-organic keys, each etched with an alien character like those around the ship. It wants four, in the right order.

interactions.response: The keypad glows a steady green: access granted. The terminal is unlocked.
The keypad is already green and the terminal unlocked. No need to enter the code again.
"Open sesame." The keypad, which has never heard of Ali Baba, stays shut.

objects.name: Processing Status
objects.description: A small monitor showing processing status and system diagnostics.

then.text: A green schematic of pathways and nodes, locked to this diagnostic view.
A processing queue now. One entry, 'XY-97-A | C44', reads 'INTAKE PENDING'. That's my tag. Next on my schedule: Neural Integration. No thank you.

interactions.response: The same warm, damp membrane as the main screen. The keypad controls it.
I glare at the processing queue. The queue, being a list, glares back without blinking.

objects.name: Specimen Registry
objects.description: A small monitor showing specimen classification records.

then.text: Rows of alien characters and numbers: a specimen registry, locked behind the same code as the main terminal.
Under 'SOL-3', seventeen Earth species: Felis catus, Canis familiaris, Homo sapiens... They've been sampling us for years. The black cat in the corridor escaped, like me.

interactions.response: I can't work this display directly. The keypad controls all the terminal's screens.
"Show me what you've got." What it's got is a lock symbol. Fair enough.

then.text: The registry reads my tag: XY-97-A, C44, Homo sapiens, SOL-3. 'Unusual cognitive resistance. Recommend accelerated processing.' I'm flattered, and terrified.

objects.name: Specimen Drawers
objects.description: Walls of drawers holding failed specimens. Most are sealed. One is partly open.

then.text: I squeeze into an empty drawer and pull it shut. Click. Click. Click. The footsteps come in, stop, and go. I wait a long time before climbing out.
Drawers floor to ceiling, each big enough for a body. The open one holds a membrane-wrapped shape about my size. It didn't survive collection.
Inside, a creature built much like me. Different species, close enough to be unsettling. It didn't make it. I nearly didn't either.
"How many have they processed?" The drawers just go on and on.
Drawers are for opening, not carrying off. Even on an alien ship, I'm fairly sure of that.

objects.name: Autopsy Slab
objects.description: A central examination slab with drainage channels and overhead lights.

then.text: A dissection slab, draining to the recycling vats, its lights aimed at a torso that isn't there. Freshly cleaned. Whoever runs this place is tidy.
A thin film coats the slab. I wipe my fingers on my suit and think about something else.
"I don't want to know what happened here." The drainage grooves tell me anyway.
The slab is cabled to the floor. I'm not getting any closer than I have to.

objects.name: Recycling Vats
objects.description: Large vats where failed specimens are dissolved and reclaimed.

then.text: Three vats of bubbling green. Failed specimens become hull, gardens and instruments. Nothing is wasted, and nobody leaves.
The heat off the rim warns me away. I listen to it.
The vats gurgle, almost like a stomach. They really don't waste anything.
I consider shoving a vat. Then I consider what's in it. I leave it exactly where it is.

objects.name: Severed Neural Tendril
objects.description: A severed length of neural tendril, torn loose when this section was damaged.

then.text: A torn length of neural tendril. The cut end still pulses with bio-electricity. It's gross. It might also be useful.
Warm and damp, like a severed worm, and it makes my fingers tingle. Plugged into the right port, it might get me into something keyed to their biology.
"A bit of the ship's nervous system." It twitches, as if it heard me.
It's pinned down with thin metal spines and squirms weakly against them.

objects.name: Nutrient Dispenser
objects.description: A dispenser that drips grey nutrient paste into the troughs on a timer.

then.text: An arm squirts grey slurry into the troughs on a timer. It smells like wet cardboard and pennies. Sustenance, barely.
I fill a tube with grey paste. Wet cardboard and pennies. On a ship this hungry, food is currency.
I push the dispenser. It squelches. I stop pushing the dispenser.
Pale green fluid still cycles through the tubes. Something here is still being fed.

objects.name: Feeding Troughs
objects.description: Long troughs of grey nutrient paste for living specimens.

then.text: Half-eaten paste, topped up automatically. Fresh scoop marks: something fed here recently.
Thick, lukewarm, faintly coppery. I wipe my finger on my suit.
They're dips in the floor. I can't move a dip. I'd look silly trying.
"What did they feed in here?" Something bigger than me, and the scrape marks say it didn't come willingly.

objects.name: Specimen Enclosures
objects.description: Small enclosures behind shimmering energy barriers, holding living specimens.

then.text: The barriers are down and the middle enclosure stands empty. The override opened these too, and the Keth-Vari didn't wait around.
Behind flickering barriers pace a dog-like thing with too many legs and something mostly tentacles. They watch me like another prisoner, which I am.
I make a sound at the nearest creature. It answers with a low, mournful one. No shared language, but a shared situation.
Inches away, the hair on my arm stands up. Invisible barrier, very real static. I'll pass.
The emitters are buried in ceiling and floor. I'd have to move the room first.

objects.name: Scratch Marks
objects.description: Deep scratches gouged into the shaft walls. Someone escaped this way before.

then.text: Gouges in the walls: arrows and a crude map of the ducts. A junction ahead splits left and right. The right way is marked with arrows; the left ends in a deep, angry X.

I memorize the scratch-map, drawn north-up: from the junction an arrow runs EAST to a little lever, then all the way back WEST past here to a skull (bad air) and on, deeper. Little skulls mark ducts that breathe fire.
"Thanks," I tell whoever made these. They're too deep for fingernails, which raises questions.
The scratches are cut into the wall itself. Whoever made them is long gone.

objects.name: Security Console
objects.description: The deck's main security station. Screens show surveillance feeds.

then.text: I lean in for a closer look at the console...
I lean over the console and get my hands on the controls...
It's cabled into the floor, and it's the only thing on this ship that's helped me. It stays.
I mutter the symbols on the display. A few keep recurring. Status codes, maybe. Or countdowns.

objects.name: Cracked Surveillance Screen
objects.description: One surveillance screen is badly cracked. Someone fought here.

then.text: A starburst crack, scorch marks, a chair knocked over. Someone fought the Choir here and lost, but not quietly.
I trace the crack. The glass is warm, lit from inside by something bioluminescent.
Pry it out with my fingernails? I've seen what happened to the last fellow's fingernails.
The broken display flickers between a lower-deck schematic and what might be a manifest. Both too corrupted to read.

objects.name: Security Drawer
objects.description: A drawer grown into the wall beside the console, jammed half-open.

then.text: A drawer grown into the wall, jammed half-open. Inside, bio-organic key cards pulse faintly: access cards for the containment deck.

interactions.response: The cards left in the drawer are a higher clearance. Too high for me.

then.text: I work a key card out of the jammed drawer. It pulses like a heartbeat: circuitry in compressed cartilage. It should open standard containment doors.

interactions.response: I already have a key card. The rest are too high a clearance for me.
A faint label over the slot: three glyphs and a clearance level. The lowest tier, if I'm reading it right.
It slides on organic rails but won't come out. It's grown into the wall.

objects.name: Data Crystal Archive
objects.description: Floor-to-ceiling racks of glowing data crystals, each one a species' complete record.

then.text: Thousands of crystals, some ancient and faded, some bright and new. Each one an entire species, catalogued and filed.
I slot a random crystal into the reader. A six-legged, furry, clever-eyed species, a lush green world, and the red symbol: consumed. I put it back.
"A library of the dead," I whisper.
It's fused to the wall. Taking a whole library home is frowned on everywhere, apparently.

objects.name: Misplaced Data Crystal
objects.description: A crystal unlike the others: personal records, not specimen data.

then.text: Smaller than the rest, a different hue, misfiled among the specimens. Its pulse is more complex. Personal data: a Choir officer's private log, maybe.
I pocket it. Alien script and maths I can't read yet, but it looks like part of a translation key. Find more fragments and I might read Choir writing.
"Someone was here before me." The crystal pulses faintly, as if eager to talk.
It's small enough to carry, if I can get it out of its slot.

objects.name: Crystal Reading Device
objects.description: A pedestal reader for data crystals that projects them as holograms.

then.text: A crystal reader on an ornate pedestal. Slot a crystal in and it projects the contents above. Efficient and deeply impersonal.

I slot in the personal log. Dense alien text fills the air, threaded with star maps and sketches. Buried in it, partial translation keys. I'd need more fragments to finish the cipher, but it's a start.
It flickers alien text at my touch and goes dark. It needs a crystal.
"Find a crystal that fits and I might learn something." The empty slot seems to agree.
It's plumbed in with cables thicker than my arm. It stays.
I pour stasis fluid into the reader's reservoir. It whirs up brighter; the fluid powers it. Now it can decode deeper layers of any crystal I insert.
I slot in my specimen tag. My vitals appear, and a label: 'Sol-3 Primate, Batch 7, Priority: LOW.' Not even high priority. And a schedule: Batch 7 is next.

objects.name: Cataloguer Robot
objects.description: A spider-legged machine among the pods, cataloguing specimens.

then.text: The cataloguer is across the pit, too far to read its displays. My line is rigged: HAND it to climb across.
I can't reach it from this side. The line is rigged: HAND it to climb across.
A spider-drone on the far wall, scanning specimens. Its jars' data plates show alien script beside numbers, but it's across the gap, too far to read.
Up close, the displays under the jars all show the same four alien characters, always in the same order. I learn their shapes by heart. A section code, probably.
I've already memorized the four characters on the specimen displays. No harm in looking again.

interactions.response: The cataloguer is across the gap. Out of reach until I find a way over.

then.text: Up close, the displays under the jars all show the same four alien characters, always in the same order. I learn their shapes by heart. A section code, probably.
I've already memorized the four characters on the specimen displays. No harm in looking again.
"Excuse me?" The cataloguer files my voice under background noise and carries on sorting.

objects.name: Velith Ammonite
objects.description: Specimen 7319-101: a Velith Ammonite, a deep-ocean cephalopod with a coiled nautilus shell and dozens of tentacles.

then.text: Part octopus, part nautilus, its skin still shifting color. The green display below scrolls glyphs beside a specimen number.
The glass is warm and hums. The shell turns a fraction in the fluid. I'd like to think that was the ship.
I mutter at the shell. Its chambers glow one after another, like a sequence trying to answer.

objects.name: Kethrani Weaver
objects.description: Specimen 7319-102: a Kethrani Weaver, a huge eight-legged arachnoid predator with an armored carapace and bone-crushing mandibles.

then.text: The Weaver fills the center tank, bigger than I am, all legs and mandibles. The green display scrolls glyphs beside a specimen number. I'm glad I never visited.
I press my palm to the glass. A leg twitches and the mandibles click once. I take my palm back.
"What happened to you?" Hundreds of dark facets stare back, each holding a tiny copy of my face.

objects.name: Neural Orchid
objects.description: Specimen 7319-103: a Neural Orchid, an alien plant with burgundy petals and thick root tendrils, preserved in golden fluid.

then.text: Burgundy petals, and roots curling through the fluid like searching fingers. The green display scrolls a specimen number. The petals seem to open as I watch.
I tap the glass. The roots drift toward my finger and the petals spread, almost hungrily. It would collect me back if it could.
"You're beautiful," I whisper. The outer petals open, very slightly, toward my voice.
I keep talking, low and kind, like to a nervous dog. The petals unfurl further. Something golden glows in its throat.
"Go on." It breathes out one glowing spore, which drifts through the glass and sinks into my hand, warm as a coal. I feel, absurdly, encouraged.
The orchid has folded itself closed again. I could swear it looks pleased with itself.

objects.name: Specimen Displays
objects.description: Three glowing teal screens below the tanks, scrolling alien glyphs and specimen numbers.

then.text: The names change from tank to tank, but these four characters never do, always in the same order. A code, probably. I commit the shapes to memory.
The same four characters, in the same order. I have them by heart.
The same four characters on every tank, in the same order. They must unlock something on this ship.
The same four characters, in the same order. I have them by heart now.
I try to sound out the four characters. My mouth doesn't make those shapes.

objects.name: Holographic Planet Display
objects.description: Holograms of catalogued worlds drift above the archive, most marked in red.

then.text: Planets drift overhead: lush worlds, ice worlds, gas giants with inhabited moons. Nearly all marked with the red consumption symbol. Not dozens. Thousands, going back billions of years.
"Some kind of catalogue," I say. Glyphs scroll in answer to my voice. I can't read any of them.
I try to grab a planet. My hand goes straight through. Six-year-old me is thrilled anyway.

I hold the neural tendril to the display. It twitches, and the star map races past dead worlds to a blue one I'd know anywhere. The harvest glyph, and a ring of marks: eleven still lit. Eleven cycles until Earth is empty. The tendril goes dark, spent.
I flick the hologram. A thousand red-marked worlds spin past like a slot machine and click to a stop on a small blue one. I don't like that at all.

objects.name: Viewport
objects.description: A great viewport onto the planet below, beautiful and unaware it's dying.

then.text: That's home: North America under thin cloud, dusk rolling over the east coast. And falling on it from orbit, thin as threads, energy siphons. The Convergence isn't coming to Earth. It's already started.
The glass is ice-cold. My fingerprints fog and fade.
"Hang on," I tell the planet. Ridiculous thing to say to a planet. I mean it anyway.
It's a window in a spaceship. Moving it would be a very short-lived plan.

objects.name: Empty Docking Clamps
objects.description: Heavy docking clamps, open and empty. The wear marks outline a hull that looks familiar.

then.text: The wear marks hold a scuffed outline I'd know anywhere: the Outrider was clamped here. Jettisoned, probably; the Choir don't leave getaway ships for specimens. I'm not leaving this way.
Massive hydraulic clamps. My hands barely fit round the smallest guide rail.
"Sorry, old girl," I tell the empty clamps. I never did make the last payment on her.
Bolted down with bolts thicker than my wrist. I leave them be.

objects.name: Emergency Suit Locker
objects.description: A locker of alien emergency space suits, built for the crew.

then.text: A suit locker, cracked open. The suits are Choir-sized. I already have the helmet from Security, the only piece that fits.
An emergency suit locker by the airlock. The suits are far too big for me. But the helmets...
Three massive Choir suits, unwearable for me. But the helmets seal on their own. One might fit, like a bucket on my head.
I pull out the smallest helmet. Too big, but the padding adjusts. It'll hold off vacuum, toxins and energy bursts, briefly.
"Emergency EVA equipment," I guess at the faded label. Every airlock in the galaxy says that.
Welded to the bulkhead. Even alien ships have someone whose whole job is welding things to bulkheads.

objects.name: Manual Override Panel
objects.description: A heavily locked manual override panel for the airlock blast doors.

then.text: The panel's open and glowing. The blast doors still lead only to vacuum, but the shutters over the great window answer to it too.
Already open. The controls hum under my fingers, waiting.
An override panel under heavy bio-organic locks. The blast doors only lead to vacuum, and my ship's gone. But the circuitry might be good for something else.
Heavy bio-organic locks, built against accidental decompression. Bare hands won't do it.

The key card slides home and the panel opens. I don't need the airlock, but one control is lit with a symbol I'd know anywhere: an eye. I press it. The armoured shutters over the great window fold back like a cathedral door.
"Come on, come on." Its symbols glow politely, which is not the same as helping.
It's part of the airlock frame. I'd have to take the airlock with it.

objects.name: Sealed Blast Doors
objects.description: Heavy blast doors sealing the airlock.

then.text: Blast doors to the outer airlock, and beyond that, vacuum. Nothing out there but death. They're sealed for a reason.
Sealed tight: inches of reinforced alloy between me and the airlock.
"Last barrier," I say quietly. Beyond it: the airlock, then the void.
I push. Several tons of door remain unimpressed.

objects.name: Holographic Star Map
objects.description: A massive hologram showing the Convergence's path across galaxies — hundreds of consumed systems marked in red.

then.text: Hundreds of star systems traced in light, spanning multiple galaxies. The consumed ones glow red — there are so many they form a trail, a path of destruction stretching back across cosmic time. The current system pulses amber: in progress. Not yet consumed. Not yet dead.

You manipulate the star map controls, zooming into the local cluster. Your home system is visible — unmarked, untouched, ignorant. The path of consumption hasn't reached it yet. But the trajectory is clear. It will. You memorize key coordinates and navigation data.

interactions.response: You can't move the Star Map.
Talking to the Star Map yields no response.

objects.name: Command Console
objects.description: The primary command station, grown into the floor like a mushroom. Navigation controls and the ship's flight systems.

then.text: The command console is a bio-organic workstation grown from the floor, its surface covered in responsive membranes and neural interfaces. A navigation chip slot is visible — the ship's course is set by physical media, not software. Remove the chip, change the course.

You reach into the navigation slot and extract a small crystalline chip — the ship's current course data, including coordinates for the nearest relay stations and jump points. With this chip and a working shuttle, you could navigate out of this system.

interactions.response: The Console won't budge.
You fiddle with the Console. It accomplishes nothing.
The Console has nothing to say.

objects.name: Command Throne
objects.description: A seat designed for the ship's commander, with neural interface tendrils hanging from a headrest.

then.text: The command throne is massive — built for a Choir commander twice your height. Neural interface tendrils hang from the headrest like limp tentacles, waiting to connect to a Choir's nervous system. Through that connection, the commander would feel the entire ship as an extension of their body.

You press the severed tendril against the throne's interface port. For a flash, you feel the ship — a vast, cold awareness. Corridors like veins. The reactor like a heart. The Curator's precise footsteps somewhere below. Then the connection breaks. The tendril doesn't have enough bio-electricity to maintain it. But you felt it — the ship is alive, and it knows you're aboard.

interactions.response: You can't move the Throne.
You prod the Throne. It yields nothing useful.
You mutter something at the Throne. It doesn't answer.

objects.name: Organic Reactor
objects.description: A massive pulsing organic reactor — like a beating heart wrapped in mechanical cables and transparent coolant tubes.

then.text: The reactor is a living thing — a heart the size of a house, wrapped in mechanical supports and coolant systems. With each pulse, the entire room shudders. Transparent tubes carry glowing coolant through a circulatory system. The vibration masks most sounds in here — good for hiding, terrible for hearing someone approach.

interactions.response: Moving the Reactor would accomplish nothing.
You poke at the Reactor. No reaction.
You address the Reactor. Predictably, silence.

objects.name: Reactor Access Panel
objects.description: A maintenance panel on the reactor housing, where power cells are installed and removed.

then.text: A maintenance access panel on the reactor casing. Behind it, power cells are slotted into the reactor's distribution grid — portable energy sources that can be removed and used elsewhere. The panel is held shut by organic fasteners.

You pry the fasteners loose and swing the panel open. Inside: a grid of power cells, each glowing with stored reactor energy. Most are locked into the grid, but one on the edge can be disconnected without triggering a system alert.

You carefully disconnect the edge power cell. It comes free with a click and a brief flicker in the lighting — the reactor compensates almost instantly. The cell is warm, heavy, and full of energy. This could power a shuttle... or anything else that needs a boost.

interactions.response: The Panel is firmly in place.
You mutter something at the Panel. It doesn't answer.

objects.name: Coolant Distribution System
objects.description: Transparent tubes carrying glowing coolant through the engineering bay.

then.text: Glowing blue coolant flows through transparent tubes, keeping the reactor from overheating. The tubes branch and merge in patterns that look almost organic — because they are. The coolant itself is bio-active, a living fluid that absorbs and dissipates heat.

You find a maintenance flask near a junction point and fill it from a coolant bleed valve. The blue liquid is ice-cold despite the surrounding heat. Useful for cooling overheated systems — or as an emergency weapon. The stuff freezes on contact with warm surfaces.

interactions.response: Moving the Coolant would accomplish nothing.
You poke at the Coolant. No reaction.
You address the Coolant. Predictably, silence.
