You squeeze between the crystal trunks. They're close enough together to provide decent cover, and the crystal refracts light in confusing patterns.

interactions.response: Moving the Frozen Trees would accomplish nothing.
The Frozen Trees has nothing to say.

objects.name: Energy Veins
objects.description: Glowing veins of stolen energy flowing through the ground.

then.text: Veins of pure energy flowing through the crystallized ground, visible through the transparent surface. They pulse rhythmically — the planet's stolen life being pumped toward the nexus. The light they cast is cold and blue.

interactions.response: You can't move the Energy Veins.
You prod the Energy Veins. It yields nothing useful.
You mutter something at the Energy Veins. It doesn't answer.

objects.name: Nexus Vista
objects.description: The massive crystal nexus dominates the horizon.

then.text: The nexus fills the sky — a crystal mountain pulsing with stolen energy, energy beams from across the planet converging on its peak. It's awe-inspiring and terrifying. The air vibrates with power. Reality itself seems to warp near it, the sky turning from yellow-green to white.

interactions.response: Moving the Nexus would accomplish nothing.
You poke at the Nexus. No reaction.
You address the Nexus. Predictably, silence.

objects.name: Crystal Formation
objects.description: A cluster of Convergence crystals growing from the ground.

then.text: A cluster of Convergence crystals, still actively growing. You can see them inch forward in real-time, consuming the ground. The crystals crackle with energy and radiate heat.
The dampener suppresses the crystal's energy. It stops growing, dims, and cracks. A path through the crystal field opens briefly.

interactions.response: The Crystals is firmly in place.
You run your hands over the Crystals. Nothing of interest.
You speak to the Crystals. Your words fall flat.

objects.name: Warped Air
objects.description: The air shimmers and distorts near the nexus.

then.text: The air warps and distorts. Light bends wrong. For a moment you see double — the landscape as it is and as it was, overlapping. The Convergence's energy is so concentrated here that spacetime itself is unstable.

interactions.response: You strain against the Distortion. It doesn't move.
You touch the Distortion. Nothing happens.
Talking to the Distortion yields no response.

objects.name: Nexus Entrance
objects.description: The massive opening at the base of the nexus.

then.text: The entrance to the nexus — a gargantuan opening in the crystal base, large enough to fly a shuttle through. The walls are pure energy made solid, glowing with blinding intensity. A tunnel descends into the planet's depths. The hum is deafening. Once you enter, there's no guarantee you can come back.
You step through the entrance. The energy washes over you — warm, tingling, alive. The tunnel descends steeply. Behind you, the daylight fades. Ahead, only crystal light.

interactions.response: The Entrance won't budge.
You speak to the Entrance. Your words fall flat.

then.text: Walls of pure crystallized energy. Not built — grown, over eons. The crystal is warm to the touch and vibrates with the nexus's power. Faint patterns move through it like thoughts through a brain.

interactions.response: You strain against the Crystal Walls. It doesn't move.
You touch the Crystal Walls. Nothing happens.
Talking to the Crystal Walls yields no response.

objects.name: Energy Pulses
objects.description: Visible energy pulses traveling through the nexus structure.

then.text: Energy pulses travel visibly through the crystal structure — like blood through veins, or data through fiber optics. Each pulse carries stolen planetary energy toward the core. The rhythm is steady: pump, pause, pump, pause. Like a heartbeat.

interactions.response: The Pulses won't budge.
You fiddle with the Pulses. It accomplishes nothing.
The Pulses has nothing to say.

objects.name: Descent Tunnel
objects.description: The tunnel descending into the planet's depths.

then.text: The tunnel angles downward steeply. You can see tool marks on the crystal walls — the strike team carved handholds and steps during their assault. The crystal grows back slowly, partially covering their work.

interactions.response: You can't move the Descent.
You prod the Descent. It yields nothing useful.
You mutter something at the Descent. It doesn't answer.

objects.name: Ancient Markings
objects.description: Markings older than the planet's civilization.

then.text: Markings etched into the crystal that predate the planet's civilization by billions of years. The Convergence — or whatever built the nexus — left these. They're not language. They're energy patterns frozen in crystal. Mathematical. Beautiful. Incomprehensible.

interactions.response: Moving the Markings would accomplish nothing.
You poke at the Markings. No reaction.
You address the Markings. Predictably, silence.

objects.name: Energy Rivers
objects.description: Massive conduits of flowing stolen energy.

then.text: Rivers of pure energy flow through crystalline conduits — the stolen life force of an entire planet, compressed and channeled toward the core. The light is almost too bright to look at directly. The heat is intense. Without protection, prolonged exposure would be lethal.

interactions.response: The Energy Rivers is firmly in place.
You run your hands over the Energy Rivers. Nothing of interest.
You speak to the Energy Rivers. Your words fall flat.

objects.name: Metal Walkway
objects.description: A narrow walkway built by the former civilization.

then.text: A narrow metal walkway spanning between the energy conduits — built by the strike team during their assault on the nexus. It's bolted into the crystal walls with alien engineering. Stable enough, but terrifyingly exposed above rivers of energy.

interactions.response: You strain against the Walkway. It doesn't move.
You touch the Walkway. Nothing happens.
Talking to the Walkway yields no response.

then.text: A junction where three energy conduits merge into one larger flow. The energy pulses sync here, creating a brief gap between surges. With precise timing, you could cross.
You watch the pulse pattern... wait for the gap... and dash across. The goggles protect your eyes from the blinding flash as the next pulse surges past, inches from your back.
The energy is blinding without eye protection. You can't time your crossing if you can't see the pulse patterns.

interactions.response: The Junction won't budge.
You speak to the Junction. Your words fall flat.

objects.name: Energy Tap
objects.description: A point where raw Convergence energy can be sampled.

then.text: A maintenance tap on the conduit — the strike team installed it to study the energy flow. A small sample could be extracted here, though handling raw Convergence energy is incredibly dangerous.

Using the dampener to suppress the energy's intensity, you carefully extract a small sample into a containment vial. The energy writhes inside, alive and furious. Pure Convergence energy — the most dangerous substance you've ever held.
You reach for the tap and immediately recoil — the energy singes your fingers even at a distance. You need something to suppress the energy intensity before handling it.

interactions.response: You strain against the Energy Tap. It doesn't move.
You address the Energy Tap. Predictably, silence.

objects.name: Heat Shimmer
objects.description: Waves of intense heat rising from the energy conduits.

then.text: Waves of heat rise from the energy conduits, distorting the air. The temperature here is extreme — the energy of a planet compressed into flowing rivers. The walkways stay cooler thanks to alien thermal shielding, but step off them and you'd cook in seconds.

interactions.response: The Heat is firmly in place.
You run your hands over the Heat. Nothing of interest.
You speak to the Heat. Your words fall flat.

objects.name: Harvesting Apparatus
objects.description: The massive machine that drains the planet.

then.text: The harvesting apparatus — a massive structure of crystal and dark unknown matter. Energy rivers flow into it from every direction, compressed into a single beam that fires upward through the nexus into space. This is the machine that kills planets. It's ancient, alien, and terrifyingly beautiful. The sound it makes is like a choir singing in frequencies that hurt.

You place the countermeasure at the apparatus's energy intake. The weapon activates — channeling the Convergence's own energy back on itself. The apparatus shudders. The beam wavers. Crystal cracks spread from the contact point. The machine that kills planets is dying.

interactions.response: The Apparatus won't budge.
You fiddle with the Apparatus. It accomplishes nothing.
The Apparatus has nothing to say.

objects.name: Energy Beam
objects.description: A concentrated beam of stolen energy firing into space.

then.text: A beam of compressed planetary energy, impossibly bright, firing straight up through the nexus into orbit and beyond. This is the Convergence's pipeline — stolen life force transmitted to the greater entity somewhere in deep space. The beam crackles and roars.

interactions.response: You can't move the Beam.
You prod the Beam. It yields nothing useful.
You mutter something at the Beam. It doesn't answer.

objects.name: Crystal Cathedral
objects.description: Crystal formations surrounding the apparatus like a cathedral.

then.text: Natural crystal formations rising around the apparatus like the pillars of a cathedral. They amplify and direct the energy flow. Some are large enough to hide behind — if you can tolerate the vibration.
You press yourself against the base of a crystal pillar. The vibration rattles your teeth, but the crystal's refractive properties make you nearly invisible in the ambient light.

interactions.response: Moving the Crystal Cathedral would accomplish nothing.
The Crystal Cathedral has nothing to say.

objects.name: Apparatus Base
objects.description: The base of the harvesting machine, where components can be accessed.

then.text: The base of the apparatus — where energy inputs connect. Access panels and maintenance ports are visible, some pried open by the strike team. This is where the countermeasure would need to be placed to reverse the energy flow.

interactions.response: You can't move the Base.
You prod the Base. It yields nothing useful.
You mutter something at the Base. It doesn't answer.

objects.name: Countermeasure Slot
objects.description: A slot at the apparatus base where the countermeasure fits.

then.text: An access point at the base of the apparatus — shaped to accept the countermeasure weapon. The strike team created this interface before they were overwhelmed. The slot leads directly to the apparatus's energy intake.

interactions.response: Moving the Weapon Slot would accomplish nothing.
You poke at the Weapon Slot. No reaction.
You address the Weapon Slot. Predictably, silence.

objects.name: Choir Consoles
objects.description: Bio-organic Choir technology layered over ancient controls.

then.text: Choir consoles — bio-organic interfaces grafted onto the nexus's ancient architecture. Fleshy buttons, tendon-cables, screens displaying the harvesting grid status. These are how the Choir manages the operation from day to day. More familiar technology than the ancient controls.

The universal interface bridges the gap between your capabilities and the Choir's controls. Displays translate to comprehensible data. You can now access the harvesting grid management — redirect siphons, shut down sectors, or...
The bio-organic controls don't respond to your touch — they're keyed to Choir physiology. You need an interface adapter.

interactions.response: The Choir Tech is firmly in place.
You mutter something at the Choir Tech. It doesn't answer.

objects.name: Ancient Controls
objects.description: Primordial crystalline controls from the Convergence itself.

then.text: Controls older than the planet's civilization — older than most stars. Pure crystal interfaces that respond to energy patterns, not physical touch. These are the Convergence's own controls, from before it enslaved the Choir to do its work. They're incomprehensible.

The core interface module resonates with the ancient controls — it was designed for exactly this. The crystal interfaces light up, responding to the module's energy signature. You now have direct access to the Convergence's own systems. The power is staggering. And dangerous.

interactions.response: Moving the Ancient Controls would accomplish nothing.
You poke at the Ancient Controls. No reaction.
You address the Ancient Controls. Predictably, silence.

objects.name: Harvesting Display
objects.description: Holographic display showing the planet's energy harvesting grid.

then.text: A holographic display showing the planet in real-time. Siphon towers, energy conduits, and the nexus are all highlighted. The planet is nearly 70% drained. At current rates, it has weeks left. The harvesting is accelerating.

interactions.response: The Display is firmly in place.
You run your hands over the Display. Nothing of interest.
You speak to the Display. Your words fall flat.

objects.name: Spire Interface Terminal
objects.description: The primary control interface for the nexus.

then.text: The primary nexus interface — where harvesting can be managed, redirected, or shut down. Currently locked behind a Convergence-era security system. The lock is crystalline, responding to specific energy patterns.

With the Choir consoles bridged, you can access the spire interface. The full scope of the harvesting operation is now at your fingertips. You could shut it down. Redirect it. Overload it. The choice is yours.

interactions.response: You strain against the Interface. It doesn't move.
You address the Interface. Predictably, silence.

then.text: A crystalline lock mechanism — the Convergence's own security. No keyhole, no code entry. It responds to specific energy patterns. The core interface module might be able to interface with it.
The ancient key resonates with the lock. Crystal patterns align and the mechanism opens, revealing deeper sections of the nexus — including the stasis gallery and the core chamber.

interactions.response: The Lock is firmly in place.
You run your hands over the Lock. Nothing of interest.
You speak to the Lock. Your words fall flat.

objects.name: Ancient Specimens
objects.description: Beings from billions of years ago, preserved in crystal.

then.text: Dozens of crystal pillars, each containing a perfectly preserved being from a different consumed world. The specimens span billions of years of galactic history — from simple organisms to extraordinarily complex beings. Each one was the last of its kind. This is the Convergence's trophy room.

interactions.response: You strain against the Specimens. It doesn't move.
You touch the Specimens. Nothing happens.
Talking to the Specimens yields no response.

objects.name: Frozen Inhabitant
objects.description: A four-armed being frozen in crystal, mouth open in a scream.

then.text: One of the planet's former inhabitants — tall, four-armed — frozen in crystal. Their mouth is open in a scream. Their four arms are raised in a gesture of defiance. They were alive when the crystal took them. This is what the Convergence does: it preserves what it destroys, like pressing flowers from a garden it burned.
"I'm sorry," you whisper to the frozen figure. "I'm going to try to stop this. I promise." The crystal vibrates faintly. Probably just the nexus's energy. Probably.

interactions.response: The Inhabitant won't budge.
You fiddle with the Inhabitant. It accomplishes nothing.

objects.name: Gallery Pedestal
objects.description: A pedestal with a crystal key on it.

then.text: A pedestal at the gallery's center, holding an ornate crystal key. It's different from anything the planet's inhabitants made — this is Convergence craftsmanship, ancient beyond measure. It likely opens the deepest sections of the nexus.
You take the ancient key. It's warm and vibrates slightly in your hand, resonating with the nexus's energy. With this, the deepest chambers should be accessible.

interactions.response: You strain against the Pedestal. It doesn't move.
You touch the Pedestal. Nothing happens.
Talking to the Pedestal yields no response.

objects.name: Oldest Specimen
objects.description: The very first specimen, billions of years old.

then.text: The oldest specimen in the gallery — a simple, almost formless organism preserved in crystal that has yellowed with incomprehensible age. This was the first being the Convergence ever collected, from the first world it ever consumed. Billions of years ago. The Convergence has been doing this since before complex life existed on most worlds.

interactions.response: The Ancient won't budge.
You fiddle with the Ancient. It accomplishes nothing.
The Ancient has nothing to say.

objects.name: Gallery Alcove
objects.description: A shadowed alcove between specimen pillars.

then.text: A shadowed alcove between the crystal pillars. The specimens' glow creates confusing light patterns that would help conceal you.
You slip into the alcove, pressing against the cool crystal. The light from the specimens refracts around you, making your outline indistinct.

interactions.response: You can't move the Alcove.
Talking to the Alcove yields no response.

objects.name: Assembly Workbench
objects.description: A workbench where the countermeasure can be assembled.

then.text: A cleared workbench — the strike team's weapon assembly station. Tools are laid out in four-armed configurations. Guides and notes are pinned to the wall behind. This is where the countermeasure was meant to be assembled. The components were never brought together here. Until now.

Following the assembly instructions, you fit the components together. The primed weapon core seats into its housing. The energy dampener wraps around it. The siphon crystal fragment slots into the focusing chamber. The weapon hums to life — vibrating with reversed Convergence energy. The countermeasure is complete. The weapon that can kill a planet-killer.

The workbench is ready for assembly, but you need the components and the knowledge of how to put them together. The weapon core, the energy dampener, the siphon crystal fragment, and the assembly instructions.

interactions.response: The Workbench won't budge.
You speak to the Workbench. Your words fall flat.

objects.name: Discarded Armor
objects.description: Four-armed alien armor left behind by the strike team.

then.text: Discarded armor from the strike team — four-armed military gear, scarred by combat. The team must have shed it here before making their final push. Some pieces still glow faintly with energy shielding. They went in knowing they wouldn't come back.
You crawl underneath the pile of oversized armor. The metal and crystal plates make decent cover, and the residual energy shielding might confuse scanners.

interactions.response: You strain against the Armor. It doesn't move.
You address the Armor. Predictably, silence.

objects.name: Supply Crates
objects.description: Military supply crates, some still sealed.

then.text: Military supply crates. Most have been opened and emptied, but a few remain sealed. Labels in alien military script.

You force open a sealed crate. Inside: emergency rations (millennia old), spare power cells (dead), and — a heavy key with an inscription. It matches symbols you saw near the escape shaft entrance. This must be the shaft key.

interactions.response: The Supplies is firmly in place.
You mutter something at the Supplies. It doesn't answer.

objects.name: Weapon Station
objects.description: A weapon maintenance and calibration station.

then.text: A weapon calibration station — tools for adjusting and testing energy weapons. The strike team used this to prepare for the final assault. The calibration tools could help fine-tune the countermeasure after assembly.

interactions.response: Moving the Weapon Station would accomplish nothing.
You poke at the Weapon Station. No reaction.
You address the Weapon Station. Predictably, silence.

objects.name: Alien Equipment
objects.description: Various alien military equipment scattered around.

then.text: Military equipment scattered from the failed assault: depleted energy packs, communication devices that no longer transmit, personal effects the soldiers left behind. Dog tags — or their alien equivalent — with names you can't read.

interactions.response: The Equipment is firmly in place.
You run your hands over the Equipment. Nothing of interest.
You speak to the Equipment. Your words fall flat.

objects.name: Staging Barricade
objects.description: A barricade the strike team built for a last stand.

then.text: A barricade built from supply crates and crystal debris — the strike team's last defensive position. Scorch marks from energy weapons on both sides. They held this position while the weapon was being assembled. They didn't hold it long enough.
You crouch behind the barricade. It's solid enough to block line of sight and provides multiple firing angles if you have a weapon.

interactions.response: You strain against the Barricade. It doesn't move.
You address the Barricade. Predictably, silence.

objects.name: Crystal Antenna
objects.description: A massive crystalline transmission antenna pointing into space.

then.text: A massive crystalline antenna, pointing upward through the nexus into deep space. This is how the Convergence communicates with its other harvesting operations across the galaxy. If repurposed, it could broadcast to every inhabited system within range. A warning. A weapon schematic. Hope.

interactions.response: The Antenna is firmly in place.
You run your hands over the Antenna. Nothing of interest.
You speak to the Antenna. Your words fall flat.

objects.name: Array Consoles
objects.description: Control consoles from two alien civilizations.

then.text: Two layers of technology — Choir bio-organic consoles over ancient Convergence crystal interfaces. The Choir adapted the array for their own communication needs. Their modifications make the system approachable, if you have the right interface tools.

You connect the galactic broadcast module to the array consoles. The system reconfigures — targeting every inhabited system within range. The broadcast begins: the Convergence's nature, the countermeasure schematics, a warning to the galaxy. The antenna blazes with transmitted energy.

then.reason: The broadcast reaches across the galaxy. Every inhabited system receives your warning — and the weapon schematics. You may not survive the Convergence's retaliation, but you've armed the galaxy. The Signal ending: a legacy that will echo long after you're gone.

interactions.response: You strain against the Consoles. It doesn't move.
You touch the Consoles. Nothing happens.
Talking to the Consoles yields no response.

objects.name: Galaxy Map
objects.description: A holographic galaxy map showing marked star systems.

then.text: A holographic galaxy map — hundreds of star systems marked. Red markers for consumed worlds. Yellow for active harvesting operations. A handful of blue markers for systems not yet reached. So many red markers. So few blue. The Convergence has been busy for a very long time.

interactions.response: The Galaxy Map won't budge.
You fiddle with the Galaxy Map. It accomplishes nothing.
The Galaxy Map has nothing to say.

objects.name: Frequency Controls
objects.description: Controls for targeting the transmission array.

then.text: Frequency targeting controls — these determine where the array's signal is sent. Currently set to deep-space coordinates (reporting to the greater Convergence). With the right tools, they could be retargeted to broadcast on frequencies inhabited systems would receive.

interactions.response: You can't move the Frequency.
You prod the Frequency. It yields nothing useful.
You mutter something at the Frequency. It doesn't answer.

then.text: The array's power coupling — drawing energy directly from the nexus. More power than any communications array should ever have. This is what makes a galactic-scale broadcast possible.

interactions.response: Moving the Power would accomplish nothing.
You poke at the Power. No reaction.
You address the Power. Predictably, silence.

objects.name: The Convergence
objects.description: A massive crystalline intelligence — the core consciousness.

then.text: The Convergence. Not a machine. Not a creature. A living pattern of energy and crystal, filling an enormous spherical chamber. Energy patterns flow across its surface like thoughts. Ghostly images of consumed planets flicker in its depths. It's beautiful. It's terrifying. And it knows you're here.

Through the interface module, the Convergence's thoughts wash over you — not words, but visions. A universe winding down. Stars dying. Entropy winning. The Convergence consuming energy to outlast heat death. It's not evil. It's afraid. It's been afraid for longer than most galaxies have existed. It perceives you — tiny, warm, alive — and it offers a choice.
You speak into the chamber. Your voice echoes against crystal. The Convergence shifts — energy patterns ripple. It perceives you, but you can't understand its response without an interface.

You activate the neural bridge. Your consciousness expands — you see what the Convergence sees. The universe, vast and dying. Galaxies dimming. The cold creeping in. And the Convergence, consuming world after world, trying to outlast the end. You merge with it. You are no longer just you. But the hunger... you feel it now. And you choose restraint.

then.reason: The Transcendence ending. You merge with the Convergence, becoming a hybrid intelligence. The harvesting stops — on this world, on every world. You are no longer human. But the universe is safer. The last image: you and the Convergence, looking at the stars, choosing restraint over hunger.

interactions.response: The The Convergence is firmly in place.
You run your hands over the The Convergence. Nothing of interest.

objects.name: Energy Patterns
objects.description: Visible thought patterns flowing across the Convergence's surface.

then.text: Energy patterns flow across the Convergence's surface — mathematical, beautiful, alien. They might be thoughts, calculations, or memories. You see fractals within fractals, patterns repeating at every scale. This is what consciousness looks like when it's made of energy and crystal.

interactions.response: Moving the Patterns would accomplish nothing.
You poke at the Patterns. No reaction.
You address the Patterns. Predictably, silence.

objects.name: Consumed Visions
objects.description: Ghostly images of destroyed worlds flickering in the crystal.

then.text: Ghostly images flicker in the Convergence's depths — consumed worlds, frozen in memory. Oceans boiling. Cities crumbling. Species screaming as their planet dies. Thousands of worlds. Millions of species. All consumed. All remembered. The Convergence keeps a record of everything it destroys.

interactions.response: The Visions is firmly in place.
You run your hands over the Visions. Nothing of interest.
You speak to the Visions. Your words fall flat.

objects.name: Core Interface Point
objects.description: A point where direct interface with the Convergence is possible.

then.text: A crystalline node that pulses in sync with the Convergence's thoughts — a direct interface point. The Choir's technology is layered over it, making it possible for a biological being to connect. Through this point, one could communicate with the Convergence... or merge with it.
You pry the Choir's interface module from the node. It's a crystalline device, warm and humming — the bridge between biological minds and the Convergence.

interactions.response: You strain against the Interface. It doesn't move.
You address the Interface. Predictably, silence.

objects.name: Crystal Floor
objects.description: The chamber floor, transparent crystal showing energy flows beneath.

then.text: The floor is transparent crystal. Below you: energy rivers converging from across the planet, feeding the Convergence. The scale is vertigo-inducing. You're standing on a thin layer of crystal above a river of a planet's life force.

interactions.response: The Floor is firmly in place.
You run your hands over the Floor. Nothing of interest.
You speak to the Floor. Your words fall flat.

objects.name: Vertical Shaft
objects.description: A narrow shaft carved upward through the nexus crystal.

then.text: A narrow shaft carved through the crystal, rising toward a distant point of natural light far above — the surface. The former civilization carved this as an emergency exit. Tool marks in the crystal walls. Handholds and a crude ladder. Partially collapsed in places, but passable. A gate at the base is locked.
The key turns in the ancient lock. The gate swings open. The shaft stretches upward — hundreds of meters of carved crystal between you and freedom. It's going to be a long climb.

Using the climbing pitons for the collapsed sections, you begin the ascent. Hand over hand, rung by rung, through crystal that glows with stolen energy. The light above grows brighter. Fresh air reaches you. One final pull and you're through — standing on the planet's surface, blinking in daylight.

then.reason: The Escape ending. You emerge on the planet's surface and activate your shuttle beacon. The Outrider — or what's left of a shuttle — carries you out of the system. Behind you, the planet continues to die. The Convergence continues. You survive with the knowledge of what's out there. A hollow victory.

interactions.response: You strain against the Shaft. It doesn't move.
You address the Shaft. Predictably, silence.

objects.name: Carved Ladder
objects.description: Handholds and rungs carved into the crystal wall.

then.text: A ladder carved into the shaft wall — handholds and foot rungs chiseled by four-armed soldiers. Some sections are intact, others have been partially reclaimed by crystal growth. The collapsed sections would need climbing pitons to traverse.

interactions.response: The Ladder is firmly in place.
You run your hands over the Ladder. Nothing of interest.
You speak to the Ladder. Your words fall flat.

objects.name: Collapsed Section
objects.description: A partially collapsed portion of the shaft.

then.text: A section of the shaft where the walls have partially caved in. Crystal rubble blocks the carved ladder. You could climb over it with the right equipment — pitons hammered into the crystal would create new handholds.

interactions.response: You strain against the Collapsed. It doesn't move.
You touch the Collapsed. Nothing happens.
Talking to the Collapsed yields no response.

objects.name: Shaft Gate
objects.description: A locked gate at the base of the escape shaft.

then.text: A heavy gate at the shaft's base, locked with a mechanical key lock. The strike team installed this to prevent Convergence constructs from using the shaft. A specific key would open it.
The gate is solid metal, anchored in crystal. No amount of force from your size would budge it. You need the key.

interactions.response: The Gate won't budge.
You speak to the Gate. Your words fall flat.

objects.name: Sky Light
objects.description: Natural light visible at the top of the shaft.

then.text: Far above — natural light. The yellow-green sky of the dying planet, seen through a narrow shaft of carved crystal. It's the most beautiful thing you've seen in hours. Freedom is up there. So is everything you might be leaving behind.

interactions.response: You strain against the Light. It doesn't move.
You touch the Light. Nothing happens.
Talking to the Light yields no response.
Overhead conduits pulse with green fluid. The ship's veins, more or less.
Warm, pulsing, and far too much like skin. I take my hand back.

then.text: I hug the pipes and heave. They pulse warmly back. I let go before this turns into a relationship.
Ear to the pipe: a wet, steady gurgle. Something is being pumped through the ship.

interactions.response: Metal grating over green-glowing tubes. Something below hums like a slow heartbeat.
I heave at the grating. It's bolted down, and it knows it.

then.text: The rivets have grown into the floor. It won't budge.
I whisper into the grate. The dark below swallows it without an echo.

objects.name: Drag Marks
objects.description: Deep scratches and dark stains on the lab floor. Something was dragged across here recently.

then.text: Claw gouges leading to the examination tables, dark stains beside them. They weren't here before. Something was processed while I was out.
Five parallel grooves under my fingers. Claws, or fingers, and whoever made them didn't want to go.

interactions.response: Claw marks don't make conversation. Their message is clear enough anyway: don't get caught.

objects.name: Emergency Status Panel
objects.description: A wall panel showing the containment deck's emergency state.

then.text: The panel strobes orange now, the repeating symbol crossed out: containment breach. Somewhere a very organized alien is having a very bad day.
A status panel pulses red, one symbol repeating, probably about me. Red means danger in any language. The security hub to the right might let me into these systems.
Thanks to the security console's translation overlays: 'Containment Deck 7: Multiple Breach Events.' One entry repeats with a moving marker. Something is patrolling the deck.
It chirps and cycles screens of alien text. Without the security systems I can't read it, but the flashing sections show which parts of the deck are breached.

interactions.response: "Status report?" The panel chirps once, which I decide means "bad".

objects.name: Organic Wall Growth
objects.description: A patch of glowing growth that has spread across the lab wall since I was last here.

then.text: Glowing growth spreads where the wall was damaged. The ship is healing itself. I'm not in a ship so much as inside something.
Warm and damp. It flinches at my touch, glows brighter, then settles. Disgusting, and I can't stop poking it.
It flinches and glows. I could cut it with the glass shard, but that might rouse the ship's immune system, and whatever patrols the deck.

interactions.response: I murmur to the growth. It pulses back, or it was going to pulse anyway. Hard to tell with a living ship.

then.text: I slice the growth with the shard. Beneath, scratched in a shaking human hand: "HARVEST. THEY TAKE EVERYTHING. FIND THE VENTS." The growth closes over it again.

objects.name: Chemical Storage Cabinet
objects.description: A wall cabinet with bio-organic seals and alien hazard symbols.

then.text: A cabinet sealed with bio-locks. The triangle-and-circle hazard marks read the same in Choir notation. Whatever's inside bites.
The seals are made for broad Choir appendages, not fingers. I'd need something sharp and thin to pry them open.

interactions.response: The cabinet is open. Color-coded racks of bio-capsules, and I don't know Choir chemistry well enough to touch any of them.
"Pretty please?" The cabinet stays shut. Choir security is tactile, not polite.

objects.name: Drainage Channel
objects.description: A wide floor channel catching runoff from the vats and the slab.

then.text: A green channel of runoff flows back into the ship's recycling. Small things glint in the murk. I decide they're pebbles.
Warm, thick, and the hard thing I find is a bit of bone. I drop it back. Nothing useful here.

interactions.response: The channel gurgles as it drains. It sounds uncomfortably like digestion.

objects.name: Small Bones
objects.description: The scattered bones of a small creature that didn't make it through the shaft.

then.text: Small bones against the shaft wall: two legs, a skull, about my size. Another escapee. The claw marks nearby might be theirs.
Old, dry bones, with scraps of the same stuff my pod was made of. They broke out too. They just didn't get far.

interactions.response: "I'll make it," I tell the bones. They're polite enough not to mention how many have said that.

objects.name: Maintenance Hatch
objects.description: A sealed maintenance panel in the shaft wall.

then.text: A maintenance hatch, its organic rivets calcified shut. Through its little window: a tangle of pumping veins and nerve-like fibres.
The rivets flex but hold; they've fused over time. I'd need something sharp to pry them loose.

interactions.response: I knock. A hollow echo: there's space behind it.

objects.name: Dark Archway
objects.description: A passage leading to the Containment Corridor.

then.text: The doorway is on the other side of the pit. I'll have to climb back across the line first.

interactions.response: A dark archway between the pod racks, faint orange light flickering beyond.

then.text: I slip through the archway into the humming corridor.
The archway's edge is warm and damp, like the inside of a mouth. I wipe my hand on my tunic.
I call into the corridor. My voice comes back flat, as if something swallowed it.

objects.name: Left Passage
objects.description: A dark passage on the left side of the feeding station, leading deeper into the ship.

interactions.response: A passage at the far end. A faint chemical smell drifts out.

then.text: I duck through the low passage. Colder air, stronger chemicals.
The membrane door peels apart reluctantly, like wet tissue.
Cold, sterile air rolls out of the morgue. Chemicals, and something older under them.

objects.name: Back Archway
objects.description: A passage leading to the Containment Corridor.

interactions.response: A wide archway at the back of the lab leads to the containment corridor. Orange light flickers beyond.

then.text: Behind me, the hunter drone gives up on the empty room and folds itself back into the ceiling.
I pass under the archway into the containment corridor.
The doorframe contracts slightly under my palm. The ship knows I'm here.
Out in the corridor I at least have choices about where to go.

objects.name: Stasis Hold
objects.description: A passage leading to Stasis Hold.

interactions.response: Behind me, the corridor opens back into the stasis hold. Amber pod-light spills out.

then.text: I head back into the stasis hold.
The archway is warm and damp, like the inside of a throat.
A hundred occupied pods hum back there. I'd rather not go back, but I might have to.

objects.name: Left Door
objects.description: A passage leading to Processing Lab.

interactions.response: A heavy armored door on the left wall. Through its viewport: examination tables and specimen jars.

then.text: The heavy door grinds open. The chemical stink hits me at once.
Something's changed. Fresh drag marks score the lab floor toward the examination tables. Something was processed while I was gone.
The membrane door yields with a wet suck.
An acid, organic smell from the lab. Specimens being processed.

objects.name: Far End
objects.description: A passage leading to Feeding Station.

interactions.response: The corridor runs on into darkness. A purple glow pulses at the far end.

then.text: I walk on down the corridor into the purple glow of the feeding station.
The feeding station is quieter. The barriers are dark and the middle cage stands open. The Keth-Vari is gone.
Warmer that way. The walls are slick with condensation, I hope.
A distant mechanical churning, like machinery built to keep something alive.

objects.name: Right Door
objects.description: A passage leading to Security Hub.

interactions.response: A door with translucent panels on the right wall. Screens glow faintly beyond it.

then.text: The panels part with a wet hiss. Monitors light a small control room.
Faint grooves beside the door. Alien signage, maybe, worn smooth.
An electronic hum from the right. Screens are still running in there.

objects.name: Back to Feeding Station
objects.description: A passage leading back to the Feeding Station.

interactions.response: Back to the feeding station. I can hear the energy barriers humming.

then.text: I head back to the feeding station.
The membrane gives under my hand, then draws back to let me through.
A mechanical hum from the next chamber. Something's running in there.

objects.name: Corridor Entrance
objects.description: A passage leading back to the containment corridor.

interactions.response: A dark passage on the far left leads back to the containment corridor. Its orange light bleeds through.

then.text: I head back toward the containment corridor.
I duck under an arch of fused bone and chitin, back toward the main corridor.
The corridor echoes back, wet and hollow. I've had cosier conversations.

objects.name: Ventilation Grate
objects.description: A heavy metal grate bolted to the floor. Warm air pulses up through the slats.

then.text: A floor grate breathing warm air. Its bolts have the same bio-locks as every door on this deck. I'd need to override the containment locks to open it.
The grate's bio-locks have released. It can be lifted now. Warm air and red emergency light rise from the shaft.
It won't budge. The bio-bolts are part of the lockdown. I'd need to override the security system first.
I heave the grate aside and squeeze down into the shaft. Below, everything is red.
The bio-locks hold firm. Whatever seals the doors keeps this shut too.
The released grate lifts with a groan. The shaft drops away into red emergency light.
Air moves through the grate in slow gusts. In, out. The ship breathes through these vents.

objects.name: Open Vent
objects.description: The grate lies askew beside a square hole. Red light and warm air pour up from the shaft.

then.text: The grate is off. The shaft below glows red and the air is moving. Everything on this deck is coming for me. Down it is.
I heave the grate aside and squeeze down into the shaft. Below, everything is red.
The released grate lifts with a groan. The shaft drops away into red emergency light.
Nothing answers from the shaft. Plenty is answering up here.

objects.name: Back to Corridor
objects.description: The shaft opening leads back up to the containment corridor.

interactions.response: The opening behind me leads back up to the containment corridor.

then.text: I haul myself back up into the containment corridor.
I brace against the walls and pull myself back toward the corridor.
My voice bounces up the shaft toward the corridor.

objects.name: Back to Corridor
objects.description: A passage leading to the Containment Corridor.

interactions.response: The way back to the containment corridor, behind me.

then.text: I step back through the translucent panels into the corridor.
I push aside a curtain of dangling neural fibres and step into the corridor.
The corridor hums beyond the doorway.

objects.name: Right Passage
objects.description: A sealed doorway on the right wall of the feeding station, leading to the Specimen Archive.

interactions.response: A heavy door on the right wall. Through its viewport: rows of specimen containers and data crystals.

then.text: I push through into the cold, dry air of the Specimen Archive.
The archive door slides smoothly, the only well-maintained thing I've seen aboard.
Faint crystal harmonics drift from the archive, just at the edge of hearing.

objects.name: Back to Feeding Station
objects.description: A passage leading back to the Feeding Station.

interactions.response: The heavy door back to the feeding station.

then.text: I push back through into the warm, humid feeding station.
The passage walls are polished smooth by countless things passing through.
A low rhythmic pulsing comes from beyond the passage, like a heartbeat.
You move to Engineering.

interactions.response: A passage leading to Engineering.
You press against the passage frame. Solid and unyielding.
Your voice reverberates off the passage walls, then silence.

objects.description: A passage leading to Communications Array.

then.text: You move to Communications Array.

interactions.response: A passage leading to Communications Array.

A faint echo returns from the depths of the corridor.

objects.description: A passage leading to Navigation Bridge.

objects.name: To Shuttle Bay
objects.description: A passage leading to Shuttle Bay.

then.text: A heavy bulkhead separates Engineering from the Shuttle Bay. A bio-security panel glows beside the door — Choir resonance lock. Standard crew clearance would open it instantly. Without that, you'd have to guess the right frequency from the panel's options.

You press the Choir access chip against the bio-security panel. It hums, reads the stored signature, and the bulkhead slides open silently. The dead engineer's clearance still works. You slip through into the Shuttle Bay.
The bulkhead is still unlocked from your earlier resonance match. You pass through into the Shuttle Bay.
The bio-security panel flashes three resonance patterns. Choir locks cycle through options — you need to pick the right frequency. Guess wrong and the alarm sounds.

then.prompt: The panel displays three resonance frequencies. Each pulses with a different bio-luminescent rhythm. Only one matches the ship's crew signature. Choose carefully — a wrong guess triggers the security alarm.

then.text: WRONG. The panel flashes red and a piercing alarm screams through Engineering. That was the cargo frequency — automated systems only. The alarm echoes down every corridor.
The panel glows green. The bulkhead grinds open — crew frequency accepted. You matched the Choir's standard bio-rhythm. Lucky guess, or good instinct.
WRONG. The panel flashes red and an alarm blares. That was the emergency frequency — distress signals only. The ship now thinks there's a crisis in Engineering.
The bulkhead is sealed with a bio-resonance lock. No amount of pushing will force it. You need either the right frequency or a Choir crew member's security clearance.
The lock responds to resonance patterns, not voice commands. Though the panel does seem to vibrate slightly when you speak near it.

objects.name: Vent Hatch Above

interactions.response: A narrow vent opening I could squeeze through.

then.text: I climb back up through the hatch into the vent exit passage.
I squeeze back into the shaft. The metal groans under me.
The shaft breathes stale, warm air. Warmer than this bay, at least.

objects.description: The ventilation hatch I came through, in the ceiling above.

objects.name: Torn Railing
objects.description: A stretch of railing is torn away over the drainage pit. The cataloguer's platform has a solid railing on the far side.

then.text: Twisted railing over a gap, the pit dark below. Too wide to jump. But the far railing is solid: something thrown across to catch on it, with me holding the other end...

interactions.response: My grappling line spans the gap, hook bitten into the far railing. I can cross whenever I like.

then.text: I back up, take a run at it and leap. For one glorious moment I'm flying.

effects.text: Then I'm not.
I tumble into the pit. The last thing I see is amber fluid closing over my face.

effects.title: Look Before You Leap
effects.reason: The Choir thank you for returning yourself to the recycling system. Next time, bring something to hold on to.

interactions.response: Hand over hand above the pit. No easier the second time, but I know it holds.

then.text: I swing the hook and let it fly. It clangs, slides, and bites the far railing. I lash my end to the stump here. It sags in the middle. It'll hold. Probably.
I could tie one end here, but the far end needs something to catch on. Thrown loose, the strap would just flop into the pit.
I could throw the hook across, but with nothing tied to it I'd just be throwing away a good hook.

interactions.response: Sharp won't get me across. I need something that reaches the far railing and holds on.
The surgical probe is a delicate instrument, not a grappling hook.
The tendril is a foot long and slick. I'd need something much longer that can catch on the far railing.
The gap is too wide to walk across. I need a safe way to the other side.
"Any tips?" I ask the pit. It has none, which is honest of it.

objects.name: Metal Walkway
objects.description: A walkway between the pod racks. The metal is warm and slightly flexible.

then.text: The walkway feels like warm tree bark: grown, not forged. Drainage channels on both sides catch the fluid from damaged pods.
The railing flexes under my grip like a thick branch. Sturdy, and a little too warm.

objects.name: Anatomy Display
objects.description: A large holographic screen showing anatomical cross-sections.

then.text: Cross-sections of... me. A human nervous system in green lines, the pain receptors picked out in red. Thorough.
Dozens more species, each mapped in detail. My entry carries the same symbol as the pod labels. Catalogued.
"I'm not just a number." The hologram flips to a note: talking to objects is a 'common stress response in specimen 7G.'

objects.name: Restraint Straps
objects.description: Leather-like straps on the examination table, worn smooth by struggling.

then.text: Thick straps, worn smooth. The buckles fit something far bigger, but new holes are punched in my size. They're built to take a lot of weight.
One strap hangs severed where I cut it free. The rest can stay for the next guest.
Impossibly strong. I won't tear one loose by hand. I need something that cuts this stuff.

interactions.response: I've already cut a strap free. One is all I need.

then.text: I slip the probe's edge under a strap at the bolt. Choir tool, Choir material: it parts like wet paper. A long strap comes free, buckle and all, strong enough to hold me.

interactions.response: I've already cut a strap free. One is all I need.

then.text: The glass shard skates across the strap without a mark. I need a proper cutting tool, one made for this ship's materials.

interactions.response: I've already cut a strap free.

then.text: "Who did they keep here?" The straps don't say. The holes punched in my size say plenty.

interactions.response: The straps are bolted to the table. I'd have to cut one free.

objects.name: Open Drawer
objects.description: A drawer pulled open at floor level. Something is inside.

then.text: A human, like me, not long dead. His eyes are open; neat surgical marks cross his chest. I wasn't the first specimen to wake up.
The dead man lies still. The marks on his chest are neat and unhurried, which is the worst part. It won't happen to me.
A human, like me. I close his eyes. Cold but not stiff: not dead long. I wasn't the first to wake up, and the first didn't make it.
His left hand is curled shut. I open it gently: a plain gold ring. I take it. Someone should carry it home.
I've closed his eyes. All that's left to do for him is get out and tell someone.
"I'll tell someone you were here." It's the one promise on this ship I can keep.

objects.name: Overturned Chair
objects.description: An overturned chair with a snapped leg.

then.text: I crouch behind the chair, knees to my chest. Footsteps slow at the door, then move on. I breathe again.
One leg snapped clean off, and deep scratches in the floor beneath. Someone was dragged out of here.
I right the chair. Underneath: five parallel gouges in the floor. Claws, or fingers holding on.

objects.name: Dark Crystal Rack
objects.description: The right wall holds darker crystals, almost black.

then.text: Almost black, with violet cores, and labelled differently. Personal logs, mission reports? Not specimen data, anyway.
Unlike the left rack, these are locked in. The Choir wanted these kept safe.

objects.name: Stone Benches
objects.description: Two worn benches flanking the central pedestal.

then.text: I drop flat behind the benches, cheek to the cold floor. Don't breathe.
Two seats worn smooth. The Choir sat here to admire the worlds they'd stripped. A chapel to their own appetite.
I sit. The bench shifts to fit me. Front-row seat to the end of worlds.

objects.name: Enclosure Monitors
objects.description: Small screens above each enclosure showing specimen data.

then.text: Alien script, but numbers are numbers: some of these creatures have been here for decades. The middle one is noted 'communicative: further study warranted.'
Weight, metabolism, aggression index. The middle occupant is flagged 'sapient, cooperative.' It might be able to help.

objects.name: Caged Creature
objects.description: A creature pacing behind the middle energy barrier, watching me with clever, sad eyes.

then.text: A lean, grey-blue, four-armed creature my height paces behind the middle barrier, dark eyes tracking me. The monitor reads 'sapient, cooperative.' Maybe we can talk.
The Keth-Vari watches me, four arms gesturing slowly. Two prisoners, both a long way from home.
Static crackles as I reach out. The creature shakes its head urgently: no. It's seen what the barrier does.
It taps its chest slowly, the way I'd introduce myself to a child: "Keth." Again: "Vari." Then it points at me and waits.
It tries clicks, whistles, a deep thrum. Then it touches two hands together and points at me, then itself: you and me, same.

then.prompt: It waits, watching me. It pointed at me, then itself. Same. What do I say?

then.text: Its arms spread wide: yes, exactly. It points to the corridor exit and mimes running. It wants me to go, and do what it can't.

choices.label: "Do you know a way out of here?"

then.text: It sweeps an arm at the ship, traces a path, left, forward, down, and mimes doors parting. The airlock. It knows the layout. It taps the barrier: it's trapped, I'm not.

choices.label: "What are they? The ones who put us here?"

then.text: It holds up three fingers and mimes something huge moving through walls, then points at the ceiling veins and spreads its arms. The Choir aren't just on this ship. They are the ship.
I nod. It nods back, a human gesture it must have learned watching. It touches its chest, points at me: remember me.

then.prompt: The Keth-Vari comes to the barrier, four hands resting against the static, waiting.

choices.label: "Do you know the ducts? Is there a safe way through?"

then.text: It mimes crawling, snatches its hands back from an opening and blows on its palms: hot wind. It taps the scorched frame and shakes its head hard. Scorched mouths mean death. Then it draws a long winding line in the air: it knows the way, and wants out first.

choices.label: "I'll find a way to open your cage. I promise."

then.text: It goes still, then presses its forehead to the barrier with a long, low sound. It has heard promises before. It chooses to believe this one.
I push the paste through the gap at the barrier's base. It sniffs, then wolfs it down and lays all four hands on the barrier. We're allies now.
It lifts one hand and holds it there until I turn away.
I push the paste through the gap at the barrier's base. It sniffs, then wolfs it down and lays all four hands on the barrier. We're allies now.

objects.name: Surveillance Feeds
objects.description: Screens showing surveillance feeds from across the containment deck.

then.text: The feeds cycle: the corridor, the feeding station's glowing cages, the dark lab. A hunter drone ticks along a far passage, the same sweep every minute. I could time my moves around it.
The feeds show the drone's sweep: Stasis Hold, corridor, feeding station, archive, then gone. Once a minute.

interactions.response: I tap the screens. Warm, slightly soft. The feeds flicker but don't change.
"Show me where it is," I whisper. It's a security console, not a personal assistant.

objects.name: System Status Display
objects.description: A readout of the containment deck's systems.

then.text: Red readouts around a sensor like an eye. Containment locks ENGAGED. Vent grates SEALED. And a deck map: the ventilation shaft runs from the corridor to the airlock bay, if I can get that grate open. Beside a red cross: EMERGENCY OVERRIDE — NOT ARMED.

interactions.response: All containment locks DISENGAGED. Red warnings pulse across the map. I've opened everything.
It's a projection. My hand passes through and scrambles the readouts.
I read the symbols aloud. Choir sounds like grinding stones. Nothing answers.

objects.name: Emergency Override (dark)
objects.description: A red emergency override button. Its light is dead.

then.text: A red button under a cracked cowl, marked with a cross: a containment override. Not broken, just unarmed. Something elsewhere on the ship's network has to wake it.
I press it. It sinks limply and springs back. It has to be armed from some other system on this deck.

interactions.response: It's a button. A dark, sulking button.

objects.name: Emergency Override
objects.description: A red emergency button, lit since the processing terminal was opened.

then.text: The override is glowing now; opening the processing terminal armed it. Pressing it will release every containment lock on this deck, including the vent grate in the corridor floor.

I press it. A wet click, then heavy thunks across the deck: every door, grate and seal on this level opens. Whatever patrols here will notice. On the feed, the middle barrier in the feeding station goes out. Four arms. A blur. Gone.

My hand hovers. Once this goes, every hunter on the deck comes running, and I won't get back up here for anything I forgot. I'm not ready. I should think about what's waiting in those ducts, and beyond them.

interactions.response: The button is dark. Every lock is already open.
"Big red button," I tell it, respectfully.

objects.name: Shaft Ahead
objects.description: The shaft continues forward into branching darkness.

then.text: The shaft ahead splits several ways. Red emergency lights flicker in the distance.
I crawl forward. The walls pulse faintly. Ahead, the tunnel opens into a junction.
the vent junction
Warm air flows from ahead. Onward, then.
My voice echoes down the shaft and comes back wrong.

objects.name: Wall Markings
objects.description: Scratch marks where the vent splits.

then.text: Scratches at the junction. Without context, they're just gouges.
These match the scratches in the cage. EAST first, to the lever. Then back WEST past here to the skull: bad air, so I'll want the helmet on.
The scratches are deep, made with desperate force.
"Which way..." The tunnels swallow my whisper.

objects.name: Overhead Pipes
objects.description: Bio-organic pipes along the junction ceiling.

then.text: Ceiling pipes branch with the tunnel. The left ones hiss with chemical vapor; the right ones are dry and cracked.
Warm and faintly sticky. I let go quickly.
The pipes gurgle back. I decide that was a yes.

objects.name: Air Current
objects.description: Different air comes from each tunnel.

then.text: From the LEFT, a sour chemical haze just hangs there: dead air. From the RIGHT, a faint, steady draught that has come a long way, so it's going somewhere.
I hold up a hand. Left: still and sour. Right: a cool, steady pull.
The left tunnel smells like a cupboard nobody opens. The right smells like a way out.

objects.name: West Duct
objects.description: The left branch of the junction. A faint yellow-green haze drifts from it.

then.text: The left tunnel. A yellowish haze curls out, sharp and chemical.
West, on the map: the long way, for after the lever.
I crawl into the left tunnel: more ducts, ribbed, red and all alike. Ahead, the air has a chemical tang.
The left tunnel's walls are slick with chemical condensation.
My voice comes out muffled in the thick air of the left tunnel.

objects.name: East Duct
objects.description: The right branch of the junction. Darker and narrower than the left.

then.text: The right tunnel is darker and narrower, but a faint, steady draught comes out of it.
East, on my map. More ducts, more branches.
I squeeze into the right tunnel. It branches almost at once into ducts that all look the same.
The right tunnel's walls are dry and cracked. No chemical damp here.
My voice runs away down the right tunnel on the draught.

objects.name: Back to Entry
objects.description: The tunnel back to the ventilation shaft entry.

then.text: The tunnel leads back to where I climbed in.
I crawl back to the shaft entry. The corridor's glow above is oddly reassuring.
I brace against the walls and back up.
"Maybe I should go back and prepare..."

objects.name: Cracked Pipe
objects.description: A bio-organic pipe split open, leaking toxic yellow-green vapor.

then.text: A fleshy pipe split open like a wound, pouring yellow-green vapor in pulses. The dissolved remains nearby say how toxic it is.
I reach for the pipe and jerk back: the gas burns on contact. I need protection before touching anything in here.
Behind the helmet I can look close. The ship's flesh has torn open here, and there's no way to seal it.
The gas hisses from the pipe like a warning.

objects.name: Dissolved Remains
objects.description: The partially dissolved remains of a large creature.

then.text: A big body, half-dissolved by the gas. A Choir uniform clings to the torso.
I lean closer. The gas burns my eyes, my throat, my lungs...

then.title: Toxic Curiosity
then.reason: You lean in for a closer look. So does the gas. Next time, wear the hat.

then.text: Helmet sealed, I look closer. Choir crew, fleeing their own ship, badge corroded past reading. No protection for this section.
"You almost made it," I whisper. The gas swirls around them.

objects.name: Deeper into the gas (west)
objects.description: The tunnel goes on through the gas toward a distant mechanical sound.

then.text: The tunnel goes on through the thickest gas, toward a distant grinding. I won't survive that without breathing protection.
The tunnel goes on through the gas. With the helmet, I could make it. Beyond the haze, a rhythmic grinding.
I push into the gas. My eyes stream. My throat closes. I can't breathe...

then.title: Toxic Death
then.reason: You held your breath, which works for about nine seconds. That helmet in Security would have looked very good on you.

then.text: The visor seals and I push on through the gas, past the curled bodies, to the door at the far end.
Air pushes against me from deeper in. Something ahead is moving a lot of it.
Grinding echoes through the gas from up ahead.

objects.name: Back to the ducts (east)
objects.description: The tunnel back to the junction.

then.text: The duct back the way I came. Cleaner air that way.
I back out of the gas into the ducts. The air clears as I crawl.
I brace on the walls and back away from the haze.
"Another way, or a helmet. Preferably a helmet."

objects.name: The Purge Heart
objects.description: A massive ventilation fan blocks the entire passage.

then.text: The Purge Heart: a duct-sized fan, five blades spinning, Choir gas canisters strapped to its hub. It drives the purges and blows the gas. Its drive is on the right wall, where muscle meets axle.
The blades are frozen, my bent probe wedged in the drive. Room to squeeze between them.
I'd lose the arm. Those blades are moving far too fast.
Cold, still blades. They won't move while the probe holds. I could squeeze between them.
I push against the wind toward the blades. One catches me...

then.title: Sliced
then.reason: You walked into a giant spinning fan. The ventilation works perfectly, though. Next time, jam it first.

then.text: I turn sideways and squeeze between the jammed blades. Fresher air on the other side. I'm through.
WHUMP. WHUMP. WHUMP. The fan wins the conversation.
With the fan stopped, I can hear my own breathing.

objects.name: Fan Mechanism
objects.description: The fan's exposed drive mechanism on the wall.

then.text: I jam the multitool into the drive and open its prongs. The Heart chokes and stops, the seams go dark, the gas thins. Far behind me, the ducts fill with breathing: the colony, crossing the border.
Muscle round a metal axle, straining. A gap in the housing would take something long, thin and strong to jam it.
My probe is wedged in the gears. The muscle strains against it, but it holds. The probe's done for anything else.
Those muscles would tear my arm off. I need a tool to wedge into the gap in the housing.
The probe is locked in place. It isn't coming out.

I ram the probe in where muscle meets axle. The Heart chokes and stops, the seams go dark, the gas thins. Far behind me, the ducts fill with breathing: the colony, crossing the border for the first time.
That won't fit the gap. I need something long, thin and sturdy enough to jam it.
That won't fit the gap. I need something long, thin and sturdy enough to jam it.
That won't fit the gap. I need something long, thin and sturdy enough to jam it.
That won't fit the gap. I need something long, thin and sturdy enough to jam it.
That won't fit the gap. I need something long, thin and sturdy enough to jam it.
That won't fit the gap. I need something long, thin and sturdy enough to jam it.
The muscle drives the fan like a heart drives blood.

objects.name: Back (west)
objects.description: The tunnel back through the gas chamber.

then.text: The duct back the way I came.

objects.name: Collapsed Rubble
objects.description: The ceiling has caved in, completely blocking the passage.

then.text: The ceiling came down long ago; the ship grew over the rubble like scar tissue. No getting through.
I push. The growth has fused it all into one solid mass. Sealed for good.
I shove the rubble. One pebble moves. The rest stays collapsed.
My voice comes back flat off the rubble. Nothing beyond.

objects.name: Skeletal Figure
objects.description: The skeleton of a large alien creature propped against the rubble.

then.text: A skeleton too big for a human, propped on the rubble: Choir crew, fleeing their own ship. A datapad still glows faintly in its bony hands.
Without the datapad's glow, I spot a faint pulse under the collar: something crystalline in a chest pocket.
I ease the datapad from its grip. The screen flickers; still charged. A Choir crewman's last record.
From the chest pocket, a warm crystal chip: a Choir security badge, still active. It might open doors deeper in.
Nothing left. I've taken the datapad and the chip.
Empty-handed now: a Choir engineer who died in these same vents. The chip might still be useful.
"You were trying to get out too," I whisper. "How many have tried?"

objects.name: Wall Scratches
objects.description: Scratch marks on the walls near the skeleton.

then.text: More scratches, deeper and more frantic than at the entry. Someone realised they'd chosen wrong.
Claw marks around a crude X. Whoever made them found this dead end first and warned the next one through.
Deep gouges. Claws, not tools: an alien made these, not a human.
“Dead end. Noted.”

objects.name: Back to the Ducts
objects.description: The tunnel back to the junction.

then.text: The duct back the way I came.
I back out of the dead end into the ducts.
I brace on the narrow walls and back out.
"Nothing more here. The other way, then."

objects.name: Crack in Wall
objects.description: A crack in the vent wall revealing the void of space.

then.text: Through a crack in the wall: stars, cool and blue after all that red. A very long way from home.
I press my face to the cold crack. Vacuum, stars, and scarred hull. Something hit this ship hard.
"Stars." My voice catches. I'd almost forgotten there was an outside.

objects.name: Exit Hatch
objects.description: The vent shaft opens into a larger chamber below.

then.text: Through the hatch below: docking clamps, an airlock bay and, is that a shuttle? The way out, or near it.
I drop through the hatch into the airlock bay. After the vents, it feels enormous. I made it.
A smooth maintenance hatch, not an escape route. It'll do.
"Almost there. Just a drop to the bay."

objects.name: Back to Fan Room
objects.description: The tunnel back toward the fan.

then.text: The tunnel back to the fan room. The jammed blades still let me through.
I crawl back through the jammed fan blades.
I brace myself to squeeze back through the fan blades.
"Why go back? The airlock is right here."

objects.name: Emergency Equipment Cabinet
objects.description: A wall cabinet with a cracked glass front and alien safety symbols.

then.text: An emergency cabinet. The symbols show a helmet and a breathing mask. The latch is stuck, but the glass is already cracked. I could force it.
The cabinet hangs open. Everything left is Choir-sized. The helmet slot is empty.
I smash the cracked glass and wrench it open. Most of it is Choir-sized, but the helmet has a universal seal. It sits on me like a fishbowl, but it locks and breathes. Good for toxic air.
Nothing useful left. It's all Choir-sized.
Helmet, breathing mask, protective gear. Safety symbols are universal, apparently.
It's bolted to the wall. Someone here takes health and safety very seriously. Just not mine.

objects.name: Carcass Hook
objects.description: A barbed bio-metal hook jammed into the lip of an open drawer.

then.text: A heavy carcass hook sunk in a drawer lip, for dragging bodies out. The tip is barbed. Barbed things catch, and they hold.
I work the hook free with a wet creak. Heavy, curved like a talon, with a thick eyelet at the top. I could tie a line to that.
I eye the hook and its drawer. "Not me," I mutter. "Not today."

interactions.response: It's jammed fast in the drawer lip. I'd have to pull it free by hand.

objects.name: Your Grappling Line
objects.description: My grappling line, hooked onto the far railing and spanning the gap.

then.text: My line, hooked on the far railing and lashed on this side. HAND it to climb across.
Legs over the line, hand over hand above the pit. It creaks and dips. Don't look down. I look down. Then there's metal under my boots.
Back over the pit, hand over hand. No easier, but at least I know the line holds.
"Good hook," I tell it. It's the nicest thing anyone's said on this ship.

objects.name: Scratches in the Empty Cage
objects.description: Fresh scratches on the floor of the open cage.

then.text: Frantic gouges round and round the cage floor, four hands' worth. Whatever it scratched, it meant nothing to anyone but itself.

interactions.response: Just marks. Whatever this was, it wasn't for me.

then.text: Fresh gouges in the cage floor: a long winding line through a grid of little squares, three squares crossed out hard. The ducts. The Keth-Vari kept its promise.

interactions.response: The scratched route. It's copied onto my map now.

then.text: I copy every turn onto my map, and cross out the three squares it crossed out. Now I know the way through the ducts.

interactions.response: I've already copied the route.
"Thank you," I tell the empty cage. Somewhere above, something four-armed is moving fast.

objects.name: Hunter Drone
objects.description: A hunter drone guarding the lab terminal.

then.text: A hunter drone hangs by the terminal, lens sweeping, waiting for whoever tripped the alarm. Touch nothing near it. Leave the lab and let it lose interest.
I reach for the drone. It is much faster than I am.

then.title: Caught
then.reason: The hunter drone pins you to the floor in a blink and hums until the Curator arrives. Next time, leave the lab and let it lose interest.

interactions.response: Its lens snaps toward my voice. I stop talking.

objects.name: Earth
objects.description: Home, and the beams falling on it.

then.text: Home. North America under thin cloud, evening rolling in. Down there it's an ordinary Tuesday. And falling toward it from this ship, the siphon beams, drinking.

then.title: End of Act 1
then.reason: Behind you, the clicking stops. You don't turn around yet. You've seen what they're doing, and you know where you're going: down there, before the last of the eleven marks goes dark. The Harvest continues in Act 2.

objects.name: Black Cat
objects.description: The black cat, sitting on the security console like it owns the place.

then.text: The black cat has followed me and taken the console like it owns the place. Maybe it does. Nothing here bothers it.
It allows exactly one scratch behind the ear. Then, holding my gaze, it pushes a stylus off the console. On purpose.
"Who's a good alien-ship cat?" It blinks slowly. I've been judged and found adequate.
I try to shoo it off the console. It stays exactly where it is. Cats.

objects.name: Hunter Drone
objects.description: A hunter drone, answering the alarm.

then.text: It's already looking at me.

objects.name: Grappling Line
objects.description: My grappling line, taking my weight.

objects.name: Grappling Line

then.text: A Choir quarantine seal, riveted bronze. Through a crack, something pale and wet stretches across the opening, breathing.
The seal stands open. Beyond it the colony has grown a taut, wet membrane across the opening to keep the gas out.
The seal won't budge. A Choir lock: the release must be somewhere else in the ducts, probably far from here.
The membrane clings, stretches, peels my helmet off like fruit skin and spits me out on a ledge. Above, a sky of breathing ribs. Below, a city.
the Warren ledge
Cold bronze, sweating gas.
A side duct opens in the right wall.
Cold ribbed metal, slick with condensation.
My whisper runs off down the duct and comes back as a dozen.

objects.name: Sealed lip
objects.description: The duct behind me is sealed.

then.text: A ridged lip seals the duct behind me. No way back.
The duct runs on. Its mouth is a ring of muscle: in-breath pulls me through, out-breath blows me back. Go when it opens.
It breathes out as I go, and the gust shoves me back where I started.
The duct breathes in and pulls me through. Air! (+3)
Warm, wet and faintly pulsing, like the inside of a cheek.
My whisper runs off down the duct and comes back as a dozen.

then.text: I press into the cold fold. The flesh closes over me and I keep very still.
I put my face to the fold and breathe the cold hull air. My head clears.
A frosted crease where hull cold seeps in. Air, and a hiding place: HAND it to press in.
My breath fogs. Somewhere behind the fold, the hull ticks.
The way I came. The walls squeeze in behind me, then relax.
Warm, wet and faintly pulsing, like the inside of a cheek.
My whisper runs off down the duct and comes back as a dozen.

objects.name: Gassed Vesk
objects.description: A worker lying on its side, its skin blotched yellow-green.

then.text: A worker lies curled, blotched grey where the gas got it, slits opening in a wet, broken rhythm.
I lay a hand on its side. It flinches, then goes still. Nothing left to fight with.
"Hey. It's all right." Its slits flutter: long, short. Maybe it's trying to answer.
Soot-black, seams glowing. Its mouth is a ring of muscle: in-breath pulls me through, out-breath vents scalding air. Go when it opens.
The vent fires as I go.

then.title: Scalded

then.text: The vent gulps and pulls me through on hot air. (+3)

I reach into the nest. Every grub turns toward my hand at once.

then.title: Bitten
