objects.name: Quarantine Lever
objects.description: A heavy Choir lever on a corroded bronze plate.

then.text: A heavy lever on a bronze plate, warning light dull red. Beside it, in Choir glyphs and scratched human letters: "GAS DOOR - WEST".
The lever is down, its light amber. Far to the west, the Gas Chamber's quarantine seal is open.
I hang my weight on the lever. It grinds down, the light turns amber, and far to the west something heavy unlocks with a boom.
It's down. The seal is open.

objects.name: Dead Vesk
objects.description: Pale many-legged bodies curled on the floor.

then.text: Three pale many-legged bodies, curled where the gas caught them, bigger nearer the door. Trying to get out, or get something in.
Soft and cold through the glove. Whoever made this gas made it for them.
Nothing answers. Far off behind the walls, something breathes in.

objects.name: Pale shape
objects.description: Something pale, crouched in a side duct.

then.text: Something pale and many-legged at the edge of the haze, eyeless head raised, slits fluttering. It won't enter the gas. I blink: gone.
It flinches back before I'm anywhere near, and is gone down the duct.
Its breathing slits flutter at me: long, short, long. Then it flees.

objects.name: The scout
objects.description: The pale scout from the Outer Ducts.

then.text: The pale scout from the Outer Ducts. It watched me cross the gas it couldn't, and now scuttles into the city to tell someone.
"I came through your gas. You're welcome." It flees.

objects.name: The Keth-Vari
objects.description: The four-armed prisoner from upstairs, perched on a rib.

then.text: The Keth-Vari, perched among the honeycomb homes. "Wall-mothers," it says, with a breathy sound that might be a laugh.

"You came down after all." Four hands scratch the torn half onto my map: folds, ducts, a curl for the court. "She wants three things. Speak her way. Give up the Choir's mark. A promise." It taps my tag. "That, first."
It clasps my hand in two of its four. "Go on. They're watching you."

objects.name: Vesk workers
objects.description: Cat-sized pale workers, coming and going.

then.text: Cat-sized workers carry food and egg crust along the ledge, breathing at each other in passing. A whole city of them.
They freeze at my voice, slits wide, then hurry on.

objects.name: Vera Halloran
objects.description: A woman grown into the wall, breathing slits in the flesh around her.

then.text: A woman the colony grew into the wall, Vesk slits breathing round her face. Her old flight suit reads HALLORAN.

then.prompt: "Thirty years," she says thinly; her lungs clean the colony's air. "The Choir threw me down here to die. The Vesk grew me into the wall to live. They chose kindness."

then.text: "Long, short, long: their greeting. It means I come to listen. Breathe it at the royal guard and it'll let you pass." She shows me: a long exhale, a short, a long.
"By moving air. They sweep the same loops on a rhythm, clicking a few seconds before they come. Get in a cold fold and hold still. In the Warren, move with the wind."
"To stop the burning. The Choir fire the Purge Core, scald the border ducts and gassed the door. The young die first. They need someone small who can turn a Choir valve. You."

then.prompt: "I could ask two things. Take my name home. Or..." She looks at the slits breathing for her. "Let me stop."

then.text: With stiff fingers she works the patch off her suit and gives it to me. "Halloran. Life support. Tell them I kept the air clean to the end."
I hold her hand while her slits slow, and stop. Below, the Warren's lights dim and the colony breathes out.
"Not yet, then." She almost smiles.
Her hand is cool and dry. She squeezes back, faintly.

objects.name: Candles
objects.description: Candles of rendered fat, burning in the ribs.

then.text: Fat candles burn in the rib-niches. Scratched into the bone, over and over, one word in Choir glyphs. I can't read it. It looks like an apology.

objects.name: The Penitent
objects.description: A Choir face grafted into the wall.

then.text: A gaunt grey Choir face, grafted among bones and candles. Its eyes open, as big as the Curator's. It is weeping.

then.prompt: "Small one." A cracked chord of a voice. "I refused to fire a purge, so they grafted me here to hear every one. The Vesk keep me alive. I am the only Choir that ever spared them."

then.text: "The Core is a furnace. Every few minutes a hot wind rolls along the north ducts: hide in a fold when it roars. The Purge Heart drives it, the fan at the Core's far end, and it blows the gas. Jam it, and both stop."
"Something long and strong in its drive, where muscle meets axle. Your probe, or the Choir multitool the Collector keeps in the Cache, in the Core's east. Be quick: the Curator will guess."

choices.label: "Is there a shorter way to the court?"

then.text: "The Heart Valve, mid-Gut. It opens for stasis fluid. Or a song." It hums a long, low chord. "Go to the valve. I will sing it open for you."
"Tell the Curator, if you live to: the Penitent still sings."
Cold, smooth skin. The eyes close, as if the touch is more than it can bear.
Thousands of small soft ears cover the walls, every one turned toward the dark at the end of the hollow.

objects.name: The Archivist
objects.description: An old, blind grub that remembers by sound.

then.text: A vast blind grub half-sunk in a pool, ringed by ears. The colony's memory: it keeps everything it has heard.

then.prompt: The Archivist turns its blind head to me. Its whole body is a throat. What do I ask it to play?

then.text: Rain on a warm wet world. Then the sky tearing, siphon beams, soil and larvae riding up into the dark. The Choir ate their world; the Vesk survived inside it.
It breathes for me: long, short, long. "I come to listen." Again, slower, until I have it.
A hoarse woman's voice: "She won't take me while the Choir's mark is on me. It's the last thing that says where I came from." Crying, then footsteps going away down a duct.
Static, then, crisp and impossible: "Outrider, this is Mission Control, do you read?" Stolen from something that steals voices. Worth remembering.
Soft and warm; the whole body hums under my palm like a held note.

objects.name: Map scrap
objects.description: A scrap of map, pinned up by the lantern.

then.text: A torn scrap of map: the torn half of the Gut, in a careful human hand. Folds circled, a curl in the north for the court.
I copy her scrap onto my map, line for line. The torn half isn't blank any more.

objects.name: Her things
objects.description: A rolled blanket, a book, a lantern.

then.text: A thermal blanket, a coverless book, a lantern burning fat. Someone lived here a long time.

objects.name: The escapee
objects.description: A woman in an orange flight suit, curled on the floor.

then.text: A woman in a burned orange flight suit, curled toward the wall, scorched down one side the way the Core burns. She tried it alone, came back, and lay down.
I close her eyes. Her specimen tag is still on her wrist, counting down nothing.
Her journal: "Their greeting: long, short, long. I come to listen. The Queen turned me away; the Choir's mark was still on me, and I couldn't give it up. I'll try the Core alone." The rest is blank.
I read it through. The greeting: long, short, long. And the Queen turned her away because of the tag.

objects.name: A fleshy valve
objects.description: A ring of cartilage in the right wall.

then.text: In the right wall, three closed leaflets of muscle in a ring of cartilage: a heart valve, big enough to crawl through if it opened.

objects.name: A fleshy valve
objects.description: A ring of cartilage in the left wall.

then.text: In the left wall, the back of the Heart Valve.

objects.name: The Heart Valve
objects.description: Three leaflets of muscle in a ring of cartilage.

then.text: The Heart Valve: three pink muscle leaflets clenched in cartilage. The Penitent said stasis fluid, or a song.
I pour the stasis fluid over the leaflets. They shiver, slacken and fold open, and stay that way.
The leaflets are clenched tight. Pushing does nothing.
I hum at it. It doesn't care for my singing.
The leaflets hang open. Beyond, the Gut's other half.
I crawl through the open valve.
Hundreds of egg sacs glow amber in the walls. The ones by the north wall are blackened. Burned.
Warm. Something inside turns toward my hand.

objects.name: The royal guard
objects.description: A Warden twice the size of the others, coiled around the brood.

then.text: A Warden twice the size of the rest, coiled round a basket of young. Nobody passes without the colony's greeting.

then.prompt: The guard lowers its head toward me, slits wide. Waiting for something.

then.text: Long. Short. Long. I come to listen. The guard lowers its head to the floor and uncoils from the way north.
My voice means nothing to it. It hisses. I need their greeting; someone in the Gut must know it.
I back away slowly. It watches me all the way.
It lowers its head as I pass.
I reach toward it. It rises, and keeps rising. I put my hand down.

objects.name: She Who Breathes For Us
objects.description: The Queen: vast and pale, fed by her brood.

then.text: The Queen fills the chamber, vast and pale, amber slits glowing, brood crawling over her. For three hundred cycles she has watched the Choir burn her children.

then.prompt: She smells the Choir on me: the tag, still counting down. "What are you to them?" breathes through the chamber.

then.text: The brood swarm up my arm and eat the signal out of the tag. The countdown stops; the Choir have lost my trail. She knows that mark well.

choices.label: "Let them take it." (show her where it was)

then.text: The brood strip the last Choir scent from where the tag was clipped. The chamber stops smelling of Choir.
She knows a lie by my breath. The brood hiss. She asks again.
I go for her. She is a queen in her own court.

then.title: Unwise
then.reason: Attacking the Queen in her own court was the Audience's one fatal answer. Every other wrong turn only sends you back a step.

then.prompt: "They choke us from below and burn us from above, and both come from the Choir's heart. Will you stop it?"

then.text: I swear it. She gives me a lung-sac to carry air, a call-stone to make her people knock on the walls, and an egg "for wherever you go". Behind her, the border into the Purge Core unclenches.

choices.label: Bargain: "Only if you get me out."

then.text: "A trade, then." A lung-sac, nothing else. Behind her, the border into the Purge Core unclenches.
I won't promise. The guard escorts me back to the egg sacs. "Come back when you are ready," breathes after me. "I will wait."
"Go, kin. Stop the heart." The wall behind her stands open.
"Go, trader. We have our bargain." The wall behind her stands open.
Her side is warm and vast. She breathes, and lifts me off my feet and sets me down.
She smells it and lets it go. She wants me, not my things.

objects.name: The drop-hole
objects.description: A hole the colony has opened in the floor.

then.text: A hole ringed with chewed flesh, opened for me: a way down into the Purge Core, about halfway through.
A wide hole ringed with chewed flesh, guarded by the young. Not for strangers.
I climb down to the lip of the drop-hole.
The young in the basket hiss. Not for strangers.

objects.name: The hole
objects.description: A long drop into the Core.

then.text: A long way down to heat and orange seams. Too far to drop. The bone knuckle on the right wall would hold a line.
I tie the line to the bone knuckle and climb down into the heat, dropping the last few feet. The line stays, swinging.
where you entered the Purge Core
I lower myself over the edge and let go.

then.title: A long way down
then.reason: The drop-hole is a long fall. LOOK down first: the bone knuckle on the wall would hold your grappling line.

then.text: Warm, chewed edges. A long way down.

objects.name: Choir multitool
objects.description: A long bone-handled tool on a pedestal.

then.text: A Choir tool: a long bone-handled rod with folding prongs. Long and strong. It would jam a fan.
I lift the multitool. Heavy and warm, made for hands three times mine.

objects.name: Trophies
objects.description: Shelves of trophies from harvested worlds.

then.text: Trophies of eaten worlds: masks, shells, a skull with too many eye sockets. On the right, a Vesk carving of a Vesk, from a world that's gone.

objects.name: The crack
objects.description: A crack in the hull, and through it, stars.

then.text: Through a crack in the hull: cold air, stars, and the blue edge of Earth. Closer than I thought.
Cold enough to burn. I breathe it in. Best air I've had in my life.

objects.name: The Curator's office
objects.description: Through the grate, the Curator's office.

then.text: Far below, the Curator plots the next purge on a map of the Core, the Purge Heart marked far north-west. It hums as it works, a low wandering note. I'll know that hum again.
"The Penitent still sings," I whisper. Far below, the Curator goes still, then works on, slower.

objects.name: The black cat
objects.description: The black cat from upstairs, sitting by the vent.

then.text: The black cat from upstairs, sitting by the vent like it owns it. As the throat opens, it strolls through. Of course.
It allows one scratch behind the ears, then stares at the vent. On the in-breath, it's saying. Go when it opens.

objects.name: Shed skin
objects.description: A shed skin, and a Warden standing over it.

then.text: A torn shed skin, and a Warden over it. The Queen's guard dealt with the Mimic. The Warden lowers its head to me.
"Outrider, respond," I say, just to hear it. The Warden's slits flare. Nobody answers.

objects.name: The black cat
objects.description: A small black shape on a far rib.

then.text: On a far rib, the cat from upstairs licks a paw. The Vesk find its breathing strange and leave it be.
LUMEN-7. A relay the size of a delivery van, wrapped in gold foil. Nine days of silence, and not a scratch on her. The service panel's on this side.

effects.text: “Panel's open. ...Huh.”

then.text: Four bolts on the panel cover, torqued tight. Gloves won't do it. My driver's on the tool mount, right there.

effects.text: “Panel's open. ...Huh.”

then.text: Four bolts on the panel cover, torqued tight. Gloves won't do it. My driver's on the tool mount, right there.
I knock on the hull, twice. Nobody home. It's a satellite. What did I expect?
Zzzt. Zzzt. Zzzt. Zzzt. Four bolts, into the pouch. The cover swings free.

effects.text: “Panel's open. ...Huh.”
“Panel's open. ...Huh.”

objects.name: Bolt Driver
objects.description: A bolt driver clipped to LUMEN-7's tool mount.

then.text: My bolt driver, clipped to LUMEN's tool mount. Right where I left it on the last job.
Got it. Clip on, clip off: the one rule out here is never let go of anything.
My bolt driver, clipped to LUMEN's tool mount. Right where I left it on the last job.
“You and me, one more job.” It doesn't answer either.

objects.name: The Outrider
objects.description: Your ship, docked at LUMEN-7's service port.

then.text: The Outrider. My ship. Small, old, and paid for.
The airlock's right there. But the job's not done.
“Back soon,” I tell her. Ships like to hear it.
The main dish. Still pointed at Earth. Still saying nothing.
Hands off the dish. Control would never let me hear the end of it.
I lean in and say “testing.” Somewhere, probably, nobody hears it.
Solar wings, clean and soaking up the sun. The power's fine. That makes the silence worse.
I run a glove along the edge of a cell. Not a mark. Nobody's been out here but me.
Nothing to say to a solar panel. I've tried.
Home. All of it, every city light still on. Every time. You'd think I'd get used to it.
It's a long way down. One hand on the satellite.
I say hello to Earth. It doesn't answer. Best conversation I've had all week.

objects.name: Inside the Panel
objects.description: The inside of LUMEN-7's service panel.

then.text: “Control, the boards are missing. All of them. Somebody unplugged this thing and took the parts home.”

else.text: Rows of empty sockets. Every module pulled, every contact scraped clean. Whoever did this took their time.

then.text: “Control, the boards are missing. All of them. Somebody unplugged this thing and took the parts home.”

else.text: Rows of empty sockets. Every module pulled, every contact scraped clean. Whoever did this took their time.

then.text: “Control, you're going to want to see this.”

objects.name: Panel Door
objects.description: The service panel's door, hanging open.

then.text: The panel door. The latches weren't forced. Somebody had the key. Or didn't need one.
I swing the door a little. It moves like it was oiled yesterday.
Nothing to say to a door. Not out loud, anyway.
A handrail. I keep one glove on it. Habit.
I tighten my grip on the rail. Habit, mostly.
I thank the handrail. Most reliable thing up here.
Earth, over my shoulder. Still there. Good.
Earth's a long way past my glove. Back to the panel.
“Hold on down there. Won't be long.”

config.title: Terminal Access
config.prompt: Eight keys etched with alien characters. The display wants four of them.
fail_text: The display flashes red. A dry, disapproving buzz.
Red again. The terminal hums, unimpressed.
Wrong. These characters are the same flowing script you've seen on the ship's labels and displays. Somewhere, four of them are written down in order.
Nothing. Guessing could take you all day. There must be a record of the right four characters somewhere on this deck.

on_solve.text: I press the four characters from the specimen displays, in order. ACCESS GRANTED. Red script crawls past two symbols I know: the cross from the dead button on the security console, and a hand pressing down. The override is armed. It wants a hand on that button in Security.

on_max_fail.text: The keypad flushes crimson and shrieks. A ceiling hatch snaps open and a hunter drone unfolds, gliding toward the terminal. I back away fast.

on_solve.text: The tones harmonize and star maps bloom over the bridge console. Hundreds of systems, most marked red. Consumed.

on_fail.text: Dissonant tones. The lock rejects the combination.

on_solve.text: The reactor changes rhythm and power surges to the shuttle bay. The alarms stay quiet. For now.

on_fail.text: An alarm blares, then the system compensates. Wrong configuration.

on_solve.text: Subsonic pulses I can't read, but the recorder can: the black box starts logging the Convergence's coordinates and orders.

on_fail.text: A burst of static. Wrong frequency; the array whines.

on_solve.text: The blast door groans open for the first time in decades, and amber emergency strips light the dust. Someone built this to last.

on_fail.text: The dials click, but the door holds. Wrong combination.

config.correct_step_message: The crystal chimes and glows brighter.
config.wrong_step_message: The crystals dim and reset with a discordant tone.

on_solve.text: The crystals align, and centuries of research on the Convergence flood the station, weaknesses included. Among the records: the fourth cipher fragment.
Lights come on in the chosen districts. Somewhere in the ruins, the Watcher takes notice.

on_fail.text: Overload. The grid sparks and resets. Too many districts for the power left.

on_solve.text: The murals glow and a crystal rises from the altar, full of futures: a weapon assembled, a bridge between minds, an escape into darkness, a warning sent to the stars. I'm in all of them.

on_fail.text: The chamber answers with a mournful drone. Wrong frequency.

on_solve.text: Seven tones lock into harmony and the ancient controls light up. From here, the harvest can be redirected, stopped or overloaded.

on_fail.text: The ancient lock rejects the combination with a crystalline screech.

on_solve.text: The antenna hums in my teeth. Galactic sweep engaged: every inhabited system in range will hear it.

on_fail.text: The array crackles with misdirected energy. Wrong calibration.

config.title: She Who Breathes For Us
config.prompt: She breathes a phrase. Answer it: hold for a long breath, tap for a short one (mouse or Space), in time.

on_solve.text: She's quiet. She heard me. Then the brood rustle, and the air fills with my smell, and under it something Choir.

on_fail.text: The brood hiss and the guard shoulders me back up into the brood chamber. Nothing is lost. Go down and try again.

phases.name: Awakening

on_enter.text: Green light. A chemical smell. My pod's cracked open, and whatever they kept me in is running out across the floor. I'm cold. Weak. And not alone: hundreds of pods, full of dead things from a dozen worlds. Something hums in the walls. This ship is alive.

phases.ambient_text: The specimen hold hums with the heartbeat of a living ship. Pods glow faintly around you. Something clicks in a distant corridor.

phases.name: Containment Escape

on_enter.text: Containment locks let go and new corridors open. The Curator's patrol has changed. It knows something's wrong.

phases.ambient_text: Distant clicking. The Curator adjusts its rounds. You have more freedom now — and less time to use it.

phases.name: Infiltration

on_enter.text: The walls turn alien, carved with geometric patterns, and the air tastes alive. This is where the Choir live.

phases.ambient_text: Subsonic resonance hums through the walls. The Choir communicates through vibration. You can feel their thoughts in your teeth.

phases.name: Shuttle Launch

on_enter.text: The bay door opens on stars and the planet below, but amber light sweeps the bay. I have seconds to launch.

phases.ambient_text: Alarms blare. The shuttle vibrates. The Curator's footsteps echo in the bay.

phases.name: Survival

on_enter.text: The shuttle hits hard. Grey soil, trees frozen in crystal, beams draining the planet, a city in the distance. Off the ship, but not free.

phases.ambient_text: The wasteland is silent except for the crackle of siphon towers and the whisper of dead wind through crystallized trees.

phases.name: City Approach

on_enter.text: The half-collapsed city gates are carved with four-armed figures. Beyond, lights still burn in some windows. Something moved in there.

phases.ambient_text: Empty streets. Flickering lights. The echo of a civilization's last breath, caught in crystal.

phases.name: Investigation

on_enter.text: Everything here stopped mid-moment: a meal on a table, toys on a floor. The Echoes are stronger, and a shape of light drifts between the spires. The Convergence knows I'm here.

phases.ambient_text: Ghostly figures flicker at the edges of vision. The Watcher's geometric glow passes behind buildings. The dead city remembers.

phases.name: Deep City

on_enter.text: The weapon vault opens. They nearly finished a weapon against the Convergence; its parts are scattered through the containment units. The Watcher's patrols tighten.

phases.ambient_text: Crystal barriers grow where you've been. The Watcher restructures the city around you, funneling you away from secrets.

phases.name: Endgame

on_enter.text: The nexus walls are crystallized energy, and stolen life flows past me toward the core. It all comes down to what happens next.

phases.ambient_text: The nexus hums with the energy of a dying world. Every step forward is a step toward something that has consumed galaxies.

phases.name: Final Confrontation

on_enter.text: A fractal crystal mind fills the chamber, flooding me with visions of consumed worlds and a dying universe. It is afraid, it is merciless, and it is waiting for my choice.

phases.ambient_text: The core pulses with thought. Visions of dead worlds flicker across its surface. It knows what you carry. It knows what you can do.

effects.text: The last of the fluid drains from my pod, and I shiver. Around me, other pods glow. A few of their occupants are moving.
Click. Click. Click. Far below, precise footsteps on grating. The Curator is making its rounds.
A nearby pod rattles. The thing inside opens its eyes, unfocused, and closes them. Not all the specimens are dead.
The veins in the walls brighten, then fade, like a heartbeat. I get the feeling the ship just noticed something.
The ship's hum changes. The Curator has found signs of me, and its amber light sweeps faster.
Small legs skitter: spider-like maintenance drones fan out. The Curator has sent its helpers.
Siphons stab down from orbit, and where they touch, the land blackens. I'm watching a murder from the killer's house.
The shuttle wreck smokes behind me; that beetle won't fly again. I'm alone on a dying world.
Reality stutters. A see-through, four-armed figure walks three steps, turns and walks back, over and over. An Echo: one of this world's dead, burned into the Convergence's field.
Collapsed shelters, a barricade, and tall four-armed skeletons behind it. They didn't make it out.
A shifting polyhedron of light drifts between the spires. It doesn't move; it optimizes. The Watcher.
The room splits: half ruin, half living city. Through the Echo Stabilizer, a ghostly scientist: '...the weapon core must be shielded before assembly or the energy will...' Then it fractures.
The nexus surges and the hum rises to a roar. The harvest is speeding up; the planet is running out of time.
A boom: a Choir shuttle crashes near the nexus entrance, and amber light climbs out. The Curator crashed a ship to chase one specimen. I'm almost flattered.
It speaks in visions: oceans turned to dust, thousands of worlds reduced to Echoes. Under it all, the Convergence is afraid. The universe is winding down, and it eats to survive.
The visions fade. Something older than most stars has shown me its fear. Now it wants my answer.
The Convergence's first specimens, each the last of its kind, sealed in crystal. Among them, one of this world's four-armed people, mid-scream. They got this far.
The sky darkens and the planet shudders. The siphons are near their limit. I'd better hurry.
Somewhere above, the clicking footsteps stop. Something is listening. (I'm making too much noise.)
Click. Click. Click. Closer, quicker. The Curator is hunting the noise. I need to hide and keep still until it passes.

effects.title: Caught
effects.reason: The clicking stops right behind you, and cold fingers close on your shoulders. The Curator carries you home and seals the pod this time. Keep the noise down, and hide when it hunts.

effects.text: The alarm is everywhere. With a hiss and a clang, the floor grate lurches off its bolts and red light pours up from the shaft. Behind these doors, something fast is clicking. The vent, now.
A hunter drone drifts between the pods, lens sweeping. It finds me before the door has finished opening.

effects.title: Caught
effects.reason: A hunter drone finds you before the door finishes opening. The alarm was your chance; the way out was the open vent in the corridor floor. (Undo, then take the vent.)

effects.text: Two lenses turn to the doorway at once. The lab is full of hunters, and they were waiting for this.

effects.title: Caught
effects.reason: The lab was full of hunters, waiting for exactly this. The alarm was your chance; the way out was the open vent in the corridor floor. (Undo, then take the vent.)

effects.text: I go back for one last look. So does the hunter drone already hovering over the console.

effects.title: Caught
effects.reason: You went back for one last look, and so did the hunter drone. The alarm was your chance; the way out was the open vent in the corridor floor. (Undo, then take the vent.)

effects.text: Something is bent over the open drawers, sorting. A hunter drone lifts from the slab and turns its lens on me.

effects.title: Caught
effects.reason: A hunter drone was sorting the morgue drawers. It sorted you. The alarm was your chance; the way out was the open vent in the corridor floor. (Undo, then take the vent.)

effects.text: In the spinning hologram's light, a hunter drone drifts between the shelves. It's already seen me.

effects.title: Caught
effects.reason: In the hologram's light, a hunter drone saw you first. The alarm was your chance; the way out was the open vent in the corridor floor. (Undo, then take the vent.)

effects.text: The grate above goes dark. A vast wet eye fills it, and a voice like a chord says: "Let the walls have it." The clicking upstairs stops. They've left me to the vents.
Scratched into the ledge, fresh: a map of the torn half of the Gut, in four-fingered strokes. Someone wants me to have it. The Keth-Vari hasn't forgiven me.
Far down the Core, a shriek, furious and deliberate. The hum behind the walls swings toward it. The Keth-Vari has bought me some room.
A shriek from the duct behind me, right by the grate: the Keth-Vari, calling the Curator to me. The hum turns my way.
All across the Gut, the colony breathes in at once. The Wardens stop hunting, the membranes stay open, and new ducts appear on my map in four-fingered scratches.

killer.name: The Curator
killer.description: A specialized Choir unit responsible for the specimen collection. Taller than standard Choir drones, with additional manipulator limbs and optical sensors that glow amber. It catalogues, preserves, and maintains specimens with obsessive precision. You are its most recent acquisition — and its first escape.

on_approach: Click. Click. Click. Precise footsteps on metal grating. Amber light sweeps the corridor ahead.
A subsonic hum vibrates through the walls. The Curator is near, performing its rounds.
The air shifts — something large moving through the corridor. Amber sensors glow in the darkness.
on_search: The Curator's manipulator limbs unfold, probing surfaces, checking specimens. Its optical sensors pan slowly, missing nothing.
It stops. Head tilts. The amber glow intensifies as it scans each corner of the room with mechanical precision.
Four limbs extend, each one testing a surface, a panel, a shadow. It searches the way a machine searches — without impatience, without error.
on_clear: The amber glow dims. The Curator retracts its limbs and continues its patrol. Click. Click. Click.
Satisfied — if a machine can be satisfied — it moves on. The footsteps fade.
on_evidence: The amber glow intensifies. The Curator pauses. Its head tilts — a mechanical gesture of recognition. It knows something is wrong.
A burst of subsonic resonance — the Curator communicating with the ship. It has found evidence. Protocols are updating.
It traces the disruption with one manipulator limb. Records it. Catalogs it. Then turns, amber sensors blazing, and begins a systematic search.
on_catch: Four manipulator limbs close around you with clinical precision. No pain — it doesn't want to damage its specimen. You are carried, struggling uselessly, back to a containment cell.

effects.text: A click echoes through the corridor. The Curator has relocked the lab door.
Metal scraping. The Curator has sealed the ventilation grate with something stronger than screws.
The lights in the shuttle bay section flicker and die. The Curator has overridden the power reroute.

special_behaviors.description: The Curator's movements slow. The sedative compound interferes with its biological components.

on_trigger_effects.text: The Curator staggers. Its movements slow, becoming erratic. The sedative is fighting its bio-mechanical systems. It won't last long.

special_behaviors.description: The overcharge device disrupts the Curator's resonance-based senses.

on_trigger_effects.text: The overcharge device detonates in a burst of resonance static. The Curator recoils, its sensors overwhelmed. Its amber lights flicker wildly.

special_behaviors.description: The Curator has been convinced of your sentience. It ceases hostilities and may assist.

on_trigger_effects.text: The Curator goes still. Its amber sensors dim, then shift — to blue. For the first time, it sees you not as a specimen, but as a person. It lowers its manipulator limbs. It will not hunt you again.

special_behaviors.description: Echoes manifest near the player, causing noise and disturbance.

on_trigger_effects.text: An Echo manifests — a translucent figure stuttering through reality. The disruption sends ripples through the energy field.

special_behaviors.description: The Watcher has detected the player and is restructuring the environment.

on_trigger_effects.text: The Watcher LOCKS onto your position. Crystal grows from the walls, sealing corridors behind you. The geometric shape shifts, its faces reorienting — each one a different sensor, all pointed at you.

win_conditions.description: Escape — 'The Survivor': Flee the system in a shuttle, leaving the planet to its fate. Hollow victory.
Destroy — 'The Sacrifice': Activate the countermeasure at the nexus heart. The planet is saved. You don't make it out.
Sabotage + Escape — 'The Best of Both': Set the countermeasure on a timer, then escape before it detonates. The golden ending.
Signal — 'The Warning': Hijack the transmission array to broadcast Convergence intel and weapon schematics to every inhabited system in range.
Kamikaze — 'The Hammer': Recall the Choir vessel and crash it into the nexus using reactivated orbital defense satellites. Pyrrhic victory — the planet is destroyed too.
Transcendence — 'The Bridge': Interface directly with the Convergence, merging with its intelligence to redirect its hunger. The harvesting stops everywhere. You cease to exist as a person.

lose_conditions.description: Caught by the Curator, an Echo, or a Convergence defense system. Returned to containment (Acts 1-2) or neutralized (Acts 3-5).

lose_conditions.message: The planet shudders one final time. The energy siphons reach critical mass. The surface cracks, continents splitting apart as the Convergence drains the last of the world's energy. The sky burns white. Then — silence. The harvest is complete.
lose_conditions.description: The planet is fully consumed before you can act.

patrols.name: Hunter drone on its rounds
patrols.warn_message: A low hum and the tick of jointed legs. Something is coming this way.

stops.warn_message: A hum and fast-ticking legs from the far side of the hold: a hunter drone on its rounds, coming this way. Get out of its way, or back into your pod.
stops.nearby_message: From the Stasis Hold, a hunter drone's hum and the tick of its legs along the walkway.

on_caught.title: Caught
on_caught.reason:
The drone's eye turns from amber to red. It pins you and hums until the Curator collects you.

The drones sweep these rooms every minute, and you can hear them coming. Watch the clock, leave the room, or hide.

on_caught.text: The hot wind arrives. It isn't wind.

on_caught.title: Scalded
on_caught.reason: Every few minutes the Purge Core's surge spills over the border along the Gut's north ducts. You get six seconds of warning: the roar, and the Vesk running for folds. Hide in a cold fold, or get south of the north rows.

on_caught.text: It turns. A click, and the whole city answers.

on_caught.title: Seen
on_caught.reason: The Vesk feel moving air. On the in-breath the wind hides you; in the still, anything moving near a Warden is felt. Walk with the wind, freeze in the still, use the pillar and alcove shadows. You start again from the ledge.

warnings.message: Your chest is burning. Find air soon: a cold fold, a room with air, or a breathing duct on its in-breath.
Your heart is pounding in your ears. One breath left.

on_empty.text: The edges of the duct go grey, then black.

on_empty.title: Out of air
on_empty.reason: You blacked out. The colony breathes most of the Gut's air, so every screen costs a breath. Plan fold to fold, LISTEN for cold air (one breath, but it tells you where), and take breathing ducts on the in-breath.

warnings.message: The hum behind the walls is very loud and the heat seams are white. Two more moves.

on_empty.text: Every seam in the Core goes white at once.

on_empty.title: Purged
on_empty.reason: The Curator reached the controls first and fired the purge. The race always starts the same: from where it turns, take the shortest way to the Purge Heart (count it on your map) and jam it with the probe or the Choir multitool.

phases.message: The lung breathes in. A wind rushes through the city.
The air goes still. Anything that moves now can be felt.

pursuers.name: The Curator
pursuers.hum_message: A low hum, right behind the grate. Something very large has stopped on the other side. Leave, or hold your breath, NOW.
pursuers.lost_message: A long grey hand gropes through the grate into an empty duct and withdraws. The hum moves off down the wall.

on_strike.text: A long grey hand comes through the grate, faster than anything that size should move.

on_strike.title: Recovered
on_strike.reason: The Curator files you under 'recovered'. It can only reach you at a grate, and it hums one move before it can: leave the screen, hold your breath (LISTEN) so it loses you, or tap the call-stone on the grate to send it the wrong way.
